One night, Tim said to his mom, "Mom, I quit. I do not want to sleep in this bed. It is ugly and old. I want a new bed."

Mom said, "Tim, you cannot quit. This is your bed. You have to sleep in it. We do not have money for a new bed. Maybe someday, but not now. Now you have to go to sleep."

Tim was angry. He did not listen to his mom. He got out of his bed and ran to the living room. He saw the couch. The couch was big and soft. It had a nice cover and a pillow. Tim said, "This is my new bed. I will sleep here."

But Tim did not know that the couch was not his. The couch was dad's. Dad was working late. He came home very tired. He did not see Tim on the couch. He sat on the couch. He heard a loud cry. He jumped up. He saw Tim under him. Tim was hurt and scared. He had a big bruise on his face and a tear in his pajama.

Dad said, "Tim, what are you doing here? This is not your bed. This is my couch. You have to sleep in your bed. Why did you quit your bed?"

Tim said, "I quit because my bed is ugly and old. I wanted a new bed. I wanted this couch. But now I do not want it. It hurts. I want my bed."

Dad said, "Tim, you made a bad choice. You cannot quit your bed. You have to be happy with what you have. You have to be grateful and respectful. You have to say sorry to me and to your mom. And you have to go back to your bed. Now."

Tim said, "Sorry, dad. Sorry, mom. I will go back to my bed. I will not quit again."

Tim went back to his bed. He was sad and sore. He did not like his bed. But he did not quit. He learned his lesson. He closed his eyes and tried to sleep. But he could not sleep. He had a bad night. He had a bad dream. He wished he had a new bed.

The dog did not like the noise and the fighting. It jumped over the fence and ran towards the boys. It barked and growled and showed its teeth.

The dog drank from the cups and spilled the water. It saw the toys and wanted to play. It bit the toys and tore them apart. It made a big mess in the garden.

Lily and Tom looked out of the window and saw the dog. They were sad and angry. They wanted their cups and toys back. They wanted the dog to go away.

"Hello, Mr. Owl," Ben said. "We are sorry to bother you. We were just curious."

The owl came out of the hole. He looked at Ben and Lily. He was not happy.

"You are not sorry. You are rude. You should not look in other people's homes. Go away!" the owl said.

Ben and Lily felt bad. They did not want to make the owl angry. They wanted to be friends.

"Mr. Owl, we are sorry. We did not know you lived here. We think you are very smart and beautiful," Lily said.

The owl snorted. He did not believe them.

"You are lying. You think I am ugly and stupid. You are mean. Go away!" the owl said.

Ben and Lily did not know what to do. They wanted to solve the problem. They wanted to make the owl happy.

"Mr. Owl, we are not lying. We think you are amazing. You can fly and see in the dark and make funny sounds. You are not ugly and stupid. You are wonderful and clever," Ben said.

The owl looked at Ben and Lily. He saw that they were sincere. He felt a little bit better.

"Really? You think so?" the owl said.

"Yes, we do. We are sorry for looking in your home. We respect your privacy. We want to be your friends," Lily said.

The owl smiled. He felt a lot better.

"Thank you. You are very kind and polite. I am sorry for being grumpy. I want to be your friends too," the owl said.

Ben and Lily smiled. They solved the problem. They made a new friend. They played with the owl until it was time to go home. They said goodbye and promised to visit again. The owl waved and thanked them. He was happy.

But when she got closer, she saw something move on the daisy. It was a big black spider. Sara was frightened. She screamed and dropped the daisy.

"Help! Help! A spider!" she cried.

Ben heard her and came running. He saw the spider on the ground. He was not frightened. He liked spiders. He picked up the spider gently and looked at it.

"It's okay, Sara. It's just a spider. It won't hurt you. Look, it has eight legs and eight eyes. It's very cool," he said.

He held the spider out to Sara. Sara looked at it. She saw its legs and eyes. She was still frightened, but also curious.

"Can I touch it?" she asked.

"Sure, but be careful. Don't squeeze it," Ben said.

He put the spider on his hand and let Sara touch it. Sara felt its hairy legs tickle her finger. She smiled.

"It's not so bad," she said.

The spider crawled back to Ben's hand. Ben put it back on the daisy.

"Bye, spider. Thanks for letting us see you," he said.

The spider did not reply. It just sat on the daisy and waited for a fly. Sara and Ben waved to it and went to look for more bugs and flowers. They had fun in the garden.

The spider felt sorry for Anna. He remembered how he felt when he was alone and had no one to talk to. He said, "Well, maybe you can be my friend. But you have to be careful and gentle. And you have to listen to me and do what I say."

Anna smiled and nodded. She was happy and excited. She said, "Thank you, spider. I will be careful and gentle. And I will listen to you and do what you say. What is your name?"

The spider said, "My name is Bob. What is yours?"

Anna said, "My name is Anna. Nice to meet you, Bob."

And that is how Anna and Bob became friends. They talked and played and learned from each other. Anna learned how to make a cobweb and Bob learned how to be less shy. They both felt less lonely and more happy. And they both looked at the garden and the sky and saw more beauty and wonder.

"No, it's mine!" Lila said. She held the doll tight and twisted Mira's arm.

"Ow, that hurts!" Mira cried. She twisted Lila's hair.

"Stop it, you two!" their mom said. She came into the room and saw them fighting. She took the doll from them and put it on a shelf. "You are being very selfish. You can't share the doll, so you can't play with it. Go to your rooms and think about what you did."

Mira and Lila were sad and angry. They went to their rooms and slammed the doors. They did not talk to each other or say sorry.

The next morning, Mira woke up early. She looked out the window and saw the sunrise. It was very beautiful, with pink and orange colors. She wished she could share it with Lila. She remembered how they used to watch the sunrise together and hug each other.

She felt sorry for twisting Lila's hair. She decided to say sorry and make up with her sister. She knocked on Lila's door and opened it.

"Lila, I'm sorry for fighting with you. I love you. Do you want to see the sunrise with me?" she said.

Lila was also awake. She looked at Mira and smiled. She felt sorry for twisting Mira's arm. She decided to say sorry and make up with her sister.

"Mira, I'm sorry for fighting with you. I love you too. Yes, I want to see the sunrise with you." she said.

They hugged each other and went to the window. They watched the sunrise and felt happy. They learned that sharing is better than being selfish. They also learned that saying sorry is important when they hurt someone. They thanked their mom for teaching them a lesson. They promised to share the doll and play nicely. Their mom was proud of them and gave them a kiss.

Sam and Lily were twins who liked to play with their toys. They had many toys, but their favorite was a big red car that their dad gave them for their birthday. The car was expensive and shiny, and it could make noises and move by itself.

One day, Sam and Lily were playing with the car in the living room, when they heard a knock on the door. It was their cousin Max, who came to visit. Max was older than them, and he was not very nice. He always wanted to take their toys and break them.

"Hello, Sam and Lily," Max said, with a fake smile. "What are you playing with?"

Sam and Lily did not want to share their car with Max, because they knew he would ruin it. They hid the car behind the sofa and said, "Nothing, Max. We are just playing with our blocks."

Max did not believe them. He looked around the room and saw the car peeking out from behind the sofa. He ran to the car and grabbed it.

"Hey, this is a cool car!" Max said, with a greedy look. "Can I play with it?"

Sam and Lily were scared and angry. They tried to get the car back from Max, but he was stronger than them.

"No, Max, this is our car!" Sam said. "Dad gave it to us, and it is expensive. You can't play with it!"

"Yes, I can!" Max said. "And if you don't let me, I will make a threat. I will tell your mom that you broke my toy yesterday, and she will be mad at you!"

Sam and Lily knew that Max was lying. They did not break his toy yesterday, he did. But they were afraid that their mom would believe Max, and they did not want to get in trouble.

They did not know what to do. They looked at each other, and then at the car. They loved the car, but they also loved their mom. They did not want to lose either of them.

They decided to be brave and tell the truth. They said to Max, "Max, you are lying. We did not break your toy, you did. And you can't take our car, because it is ours. We are going to tell mom what you did, and she will be mad at you!"

Max was surprised and scared. He did not expect Sam and Lily to dare to stand up to him. He knew he was wrong, and he felt ashamed. He let go of the car and said, "Sorry, Sam and Lily. I was mean and selfish. I won't take your car, and I won't make a threat. Can you forgive me?"

Sam and Lily were happy and relieved. They forgave Max, and they let him play with their car for a little while. They also told their mom what happened, and she was proud of them. She said, "Sam and Lily, you did the right thing. You were honest and brave, and you did not let Max bully you. You are good twins, and I love you very much."

The moral of the story is: Be honest and brave, and don't let anyone take your things or make threats.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play with his toys and watch cartoons. One day, he went to the kitchen to get a snack. He saw a big knife on the counter. It looked heavy and scary. 

Timmy's mom was in the living room watching TV. Timmy wanted to show her the knife, so he grabbed it and ran to the living room. But when he got there, he accidentally dropped the knife on the floor. It made a loud noise and scared Timmy. 

Timmy's mom heard the noise and came to see what happened. She saw the knife on the floor and screamed. Timmy started crying because he was scared too. His mom hugged him and told him it was okay. She explained that knives are dangerous and he should never touch them. From that day on, Timmy never went near the knives in the kitchen again.

Lily was sad and worried. She asked her mom if they could put up posters to find Mittens. Her mom agreed and they spent the evening making posters. The next day, they put them up all around the neighborhood.

A few days later, Lily got a call from a neighbor saying they had found Mittens. Lily was so happy and relieved. She ran to the neighbor's house to complete the reunion with her furry friend. It was true love between Lily and Mittens, and they were never separated again.

Once upon a time, there were two friends named Timmy and Tommy. They loved to eat and play together. One day, they both wanted to eat a cake, but they only had one fork. 

Timmy said, "Let's share the fork, Tommy." 

Tommy replied, "No, I want my own fork. It's different from yours." 

Timmy didn't understand why they needed two different forks, but Tommy insisted. So, they decided to have a race to see who could find a fork first. 

As they ran around the house, Timmy saw a fork on the floor and picked it up. But when he showed it to Tommy, Tommy said, "That's my fork! You twisted it!" 

Timmy didn't mean to twist the fork, but Tommy was angry. They started to argue, but then Timmy had an idea. He said, "Let's use the twisted fork together. That way, we can both have a turn using it." 

Tommy thought about it and agreed. They both ate the cake with the twisted fork, taking turns using it. They were happy again and realized that sharing was better than arguing.

Once upon a time, there was a pilot named Jack. He flew planes high in the sky. One day, he flew into an unknown storm. The storm was very strong and the plane started to shake.

Lily and Ben are in school. They like to draw on the blackboard with chalk. They make flowers and cars and stars. But today, Lily is sad. She has a hurt on her knee. She fell down in the park and scraped it.

Ben sees Lily's hurt and says, "Oh no, Lily, your knee is red and ouchy. Does it hurt a lot?"

Lily nods and says, "Yes, it hurts a lot. I want to go home and see Mommy. She can make it better."

Ben says, "I have an idea. Why don't we draw a big heart on the blackboard and tell the teacher that it is for Lily's knee? Maybe that will make her feel better."

Lily smiles and says, "That is a good idea, Ben. You are a good friend. Let's do it."

They take the chalk and draw a big heart on the blackboard. They write "For Lily's knee" inside the heart. They are very proud of their drawing. They wait for the teacher to come and see it.

The teacher comes and sees the heart on the blackboard. She says, "Wow, what a beautiful heart! Who made it?"

Lily and Ben raise their hands and say, "We did, teacher. It is for Lily's knee. She has a hurt and we want to make her feel better."

Tom and Anna are friends. They like to play in the park. They see a big fish tank with many fish. The fish tank has a sign that says "Oxygen". Tom and Anna do not know what oxygen is.

"Look at the fish, Anna. They are so pretty. Do you think they can talk?" Tom asks.

"I don't know, Tom. Maybe they can talk to each other. But we cannot hear them. They are in the water." Anna says.

"Maybe they need oxygen to talk. Like we need air to talk." Tom says.

"Maybe. But what is oxygen?" Anna asks.

Tom and Anna see a man who works at the park. He is wearing a blue shirt and a hat. He is feeding the fish.

"Excuse me, sir. What is oxygen?" Tom asks.

The man smiles and kneels down to talk to Tom and Anna.

"Oxygen is a very important thing, kids. It is in the air we breathe. It helps us live and talk. The fish also need oxygen, but they get it from the water. The water has oxygen too, but not as much as the air. That's why the fish tank has a machine that makes bubbles. The bubbles give more oxygen to the water and the fish." The man explains.

"Wow, that is very interesting. Thank you, sir." Tom says.

"Yes, thank you. You are very smart." Anna says.

The man laughs and says, "You are very welcome, kids. You are very curious and polite. I'm glad you like the fish. They are very beautiful and special. But remember, they are also very poor. They cannot leave the fish tank. They cannot see the sky or the trees or the flowers. They cannot play with other animals. They only have each other. So we have to be kind and respectful to them. We have to take care of them and their oxygen. Okay?"

"Okay, sir. We understand. We will be kind and respectful to the fish. We will not touch them or make noise or throw things at them. We will just watch them and learn from them." Tom and Anna say.

"Good. That's very nice of you. I'm sure the fish appreciate it. Now, have fun and enjoy the park. But don't forget to breathe. Oxygen is good for you too." The man says.

Tom and Anna wave goodbye to the man and the fish. They go to play on the swings and the slide. They breathe the fresh air and feel happy. They have learned something new today. They have learned about oxygen.

"Sure, his name is Max and he is very harmless. He likes children and he likes to wave his hair when he is happy," the lady said.

Anna and Ben went closer to Max and touched his soft hair. Max licked their faces and made them giggle. He waved his hair and wagged his tail. Anna and Ben waved back at him and said hello.

They played with Max for a while and then said goodbye to him and the lady. They thanked them for letting them pet the dog and went back to their slide and swing. They had a lot of fun in the park that day.

Lily and Tom are friends. They like to play in the park. They see a big swing. Lily wants to swing high. Tom wants to swing low.

"Can I swing first?" Lily asks.

"OK, but only for a little bit," Tom says.

Lily gets on the swing. She pushes with her feet. She swings high and fast. She feels the wind in her hair. She laughs.

"Wow, you are so good at swinging!" Tom says.

"Thank you, Tom. Do you want to try?" Lily asks.

Tom nods. He gets on the swing. He does not push with his feet. He swings low and slow. He feels bored.

"This is not fun," Tom says.

"Why don't you push with your feet?" Lily asks.

"I don't want to. I am lazy," Tom says.

Lily sees something shiny on the ground. She gets off the swing. She runs to the shiny thing. It is an egg.

"Look, Tom, I found an egg!" Lily says.

"Where did it come from?" Tom asks.

"I don't know. Maybe a bird left it here," Lily says.

"Can we open it?" Tom asks.

"I don't know. Maybe we should leave it alone," Lily says.

"But I want to see what is inside," Tom says.

He gets off the swing. He runs to Lily. He takes the egg from her hand. He tries to crack it.

"Tom, don't do that!" Lily says.

But it is too late. The egg breaks. A baby bird comes out. It is wet and scared. It cries.

"Tom, you hurt the baby bird!" Lily says.

"I'm sorry, Lily. I didn't know," Tom says.

They feel bad. They don't know what to do. They hear a loud noise. They look up. They see a big bird. It is the baby bird's mom. She is angry. She flies to them. She takes the baby bird in her beak. She flies away.

"Bye, baby bird," Lily says.

"Bye, baby bird," Tom says.

They are sad. They are sorry. They hug each other.

"Let's go home," Lily says.

"OK, let's go home," Tom says.

They walk away. They don't play with the swing anymore. They don't play with eggs anymore. They learn a lesson. They are not lazy anymore. They are careful and kind.

Tim and Jen went to the zoo with Mom and Dad. They saw many animals, like lions, monkeys, and birds. But their favorite was the hippo. The hippo was big and gray, and had a huge mouth. He liked to swim in the water and splash with his friends.

"Look, Mom, the hippo is spraying water!" Tim said, pointing at the hippo. The hippo was using his nose to blow water in the air, like a fountain. It made a funny sound, and the water fell on the other hippos and the grass.

"Wow, that's cool!" Jen said. She wanted to spray water too. She saw a hose near the fence, and ran to it. She turned on the tap, and held the hose. She aimed at the hippo, and squeezed the handle.

"Jen, no!" Mom shouted. "That's not nice! You can't spray the hippo!"

But it was too late. Jen sprayed the hippo with the hose, and the hippo did not like it. He roared and opened his mouth, showing his big teeth. He sprayed water back at Jen, and hit her in the face. Jen dropped the hose and screamed. She was wet and scared.

"Jen, I'm sorry, I'm sorry!" Tim said, running to her. He hugged her and tried to calm her down. He felt bad for her and the hippo.

"Jen, that was a bad thing to do," Dad said, picking her up. "You should never spray the animals. They have feelings too, and they don't like to be bothered."

"I'm sorry, Dad," Jen said, sobbing. "I just wanted to have fun. I didn't mean to make the hippo angry."

"It's okay, Jen," Mom said, wiping her face. "You made a mistake, but you learned from it. Next time, you can watch the hippo spray, but not spray him yourself."

"Okay, Mom," Jen said, nodding. She looked at the hippo, who was still swimming and splashing. She felt sorry for him too. She wanted to say sorry, but she didn't know how.

"Can we buy a toy hippo, Mom?" Jen asked. "A cheap one, please?"

"Sure, Jen," Mom said, smiling. "A cheap toy hippo sounds like a good idea. Maybe you can play with it and spray it with water at home. But only if the hippo likes it."

"Okay, Mom," Jen said, smiling too. She hoped the hippo would like it. She hoped the hippo would forgive her. She hoped the hippo would be her friend.

"Let's get a ladder," Sara said.

"No, let's get a chair," Ben said.

They argued and argued. They were both stubborn. They did not want to listen to each other.

Then they saw their big brother, Tom, coming home. He was tall and strong. He could help them.

"Tom, Tom, can you help us?" Sara and Ben shouted.

"What do you need?" Tom asked.

"We want to decorate the tree, but it's too high," Sara said.

"Can you lift us up?" Ben said.

Tom smiled. He liked to help his siblings. He agreed to lift them up, one by one, so they could decorate the tree.

Sara and Ben were happy. They thanked Tom and gave him a hug. They hung the shiny things on the branches. The tree looked beautiful.

Then they saw their mom coming out of the house. She had a big box in her hands.

"What's that, mom?" Sara and Ben asked.

"It's a surprise for you," mom said. "Do you want to open it?"

Sara and Ben nodded. They ran to mom and opened the box. Inside, there were more shiny things to decorate the tree. There were also cookies and hot chocolate.

"Wow, thank you, mom!" Sara and Ben said.

They shared the cookies and hot chocolate with Tom and mom. They enjoyed the warm and sweet treats. They looked at the tree and smiled. They had a fun and cozy afternoon.

"Let's play hide and seek with the balloons," Ben said. "You hide first and I will find you."

Anna nodded and ran to find a good spot. She saw a big tree with many leaves. She hid behind the tree and held her balloon. She hoped Ben would not see her.

Ben counted to ten and then opened his eyes. He looked around the park. He saw some swings, a slide, a bench, and a fountain. But he did not see Anna or her balloon.

"Where are you, Anna?" he called. "I can't find you."

Anna heard Ben's voice. She wanted to surprise him. She waited for him to come closer. Then she jumped out from behind the tree and shouted, "Boo!"

Ben was startled and dropped his balloon. The balloon flew away and landed on the fountain. The water sprayed the balloon and made it pop.

"Oh no, my balloon!" Ben cried. He ran to the fountain and tried to get his balloon. But it was too late. The balloon was gone.

Anna felt sorry for Ben. She saw that he was sad. She wanted to be helpful. She ran to him and gave him a hug.

"I'm sorry, Ben. I didn't mean to scare you. Here, you can have my balloon. I have another one at home."

Ben smiled and hugged Anna back. He took her balloon and thanked her.

"Thank you, Anna. You are very helpful. And you are a good hider. You are my best friend."

Anna and Ben smiled and played with the balloon. They had fun in the park. They were happy.

"Oh no!" Lily said. "We can't go to the park now. It's too wet and scary."

Ben was sad too. He wanted to play on the swings and slide. He started to cry.

"Shh, it's okay," Mom said. "We can do something fun inside. How about we make some cookies?"

Lily and Ben liked cookies. They wiped their tears and followed Mom to the kitchen. Mom gave them aprons and spoons and bowls. They helped Mom measure and mix and roll the dough. They cut out shapes like stars and hearts and flowers. They put them on a tray and Mom put them in the oven.

"Now we have to wait," Mom said. "Be patient, my loves. The cookies will be ready soon."

Lily and Ben smelled the cookies baking. They smelled sweet and yummy. They heard the timer beep. Mom took out the tray and put it on the table. She let the cookies cool a little and then gave one to each child.

"Mmm, these are delicious!" Lily said.

"Thank you, Mom!" Ben said.

They ate their cookies and drank some milk. They smiled and hugged Mom. They forgot about the storm. They were happy.

Sara liked to spend time with her grandma. Grandma was old and kind. She had white hair and a white cat. She also liked to read poems to Sara.

One day, Sara and Grandma were sitting on the couch. Grandma opened a big book and said, "This is a poem book. Poems are like songs, but you say them, not sing them. Do you want to hear a poem?"

Sara nodded. She liked poems. They made her feel happy and calm.

Grandma smiled and read a poem. It was about a snowman who had a hat and a scarf and a carrot nose. Sara listened and imagined the snowman. She wished she could make one.

When Grandma finished, she asked, "Did you like the poem, Sara?"

Sara nodded again. She said, "Yes, Grandma, I liked it very much. Can we make a snowman too?"

Grandma laughed and said, "Maybe when it snows, we can. But for now, we can draw one. Do you want to do that?"

Sara said, "Yes, please!" She ran to get some paper and crayons. She and Grandma drew a white snowman with a hat and a scarf and a carrot nose. They also drew a white cat and a big book. They wrote the poem under the picture.

Sara and Grandma were very proud of their drawing. They hung it on the fridge. They hugged and said, "We love poems and snowmen and each other!"

Lily and Tom are twins. They like to play with their toys and books. One day, their mom says, "We are going to see a big place. It is called a university. There are many people who learn and teach there. Do you want to go?"

Lily and Tom say, "Yes, mom, we want to go. What can we see there?"

Mom says, "You can see many things. You can see big buildings, green grass, pretty flowers, and funny statues. You can also see people who read, write, draw, and sing. Maybe you can make some new friends too."

Lily and Tom are very happy. They get in the car with mom and dad. They drive for a long time. They see many cars, buses, and bikes on the road. They also see some cows, horses, and sheep on the farms. They say, "Moo, neigh, and baa" to them.

They finally arrive at the university. They get out of the car and look around. They see a big sign that says, "Welcome to the University". They see many people walking, talking, and smiling. They see some people wearing funny hats and gowns. They say, "Hello, hello" to them.

They follow mom and dad to a big building. They go inside and see a big hall. They see many chairs, tables, and balloons. They see a big stage with a microphone and a screen. They see some people sitting on the stage. They hear some music playing.

They have a lovely day at the university. They see many new things and meet many new people. They learn a lot and have a lot of fun. They say, "Thank you, mom and dad, for taking us to the university. It is a wonderful place. Maybe we can come back again."

Tom and Sam are brothers. They like to play with cars and trucks. They have many cars and trucks of different colors and sizes. They make noises like vroom and beep when they play.

One day, they find a big steel truck in the garage. It is shiny and strong. It has big wheels and a loud horn. Tom and Sam want to play with it. They push it and pull it and make it go fast and slow.

"Look, Sam, this truck is so cool!" Tom says. "It can chew anything!"

"Chew anything?" Sam asks. "What do you mean?"

Tom points to a pile of wood and nails. "Watch this!" he says. He drives the truck towards the pile and crashes into it. The truck makes a crunching sound and breaks some of the wood and nails.

"Wow!" Sam says. "That is amazing! Can it chew anything else?"

Tom smiles. He sees a big red ball on the grass. He drives the truck towards the ball and tries to chew it. But the ball is too big and soft. The truck bounces off the ball and flips over.

"Uh-oh!" Tom says. "The truck is stuck!"

Sam runs to help him. He tries to lift the truck, but it is too heavy. He pushes it, but it does not move.

"Tom, what do we do?" Sam says. "The truck is too big and strong!"

Tom thinks. He has an idea. He sees a rope on the wall. He grabs the rope and ties it to the truck. He gives the other end to Sam.

"Sam, pull the rope!" he says. "Maybe we can make the truck move!"

Sam nods. He pulls the rope with all his might. Tom pushes the truck with all his might. Together, they make the truck move. The truck rolls back to its place.

"Yay!" Tom and Sam say. "We did it!"

They hug each other and laugh. They are happy. They love the steel truck, but they love each other more. They decide to play with their smaller cars and trucks instead. They are more fun and easier to chew.

Lily and Ben were twins who liked to play with their big red ball. They would bounce it high in the air and catch it, or roll it to each other, or kick it across the yard. They had a lot of fun with their ball.

One day, they saw a shiny new automobile parked in front of their house. It was blue and had four doors and a big trunk. They wondered who it belonged to and what it was doing there.

"Let's go see it!" said Lily, grabbing the ball.

"OK, but be careful!" said Ben, following her.

They ran to the automobile and looked at it with curiosity. They touched the windows and the tires and the mirrors. They saw their faces reflected in the metal. They thought it was very pretty and different from their ordinary automobile, which was old and gray and had a dent in the side.

"Can we bounce the ball on it?" asked Lily, holding the ball.

"No, that's not nice!" said Ben, shaking his head. "It's not ours, and we might scratch it or break it. We should bounce the ball somewhere else."

But Lily didn't listen. She threw the ball as hard as she could on the roof of the automobile. The ball bounced back and hit her in the face. She cried out in pain and dropped the ball.

"Ow, ow, ow!" she wailed, rubbing her nose.

Ben ran to her and hugged her. He picked up the ball and put it in his pocket.

"I'm sorry, Lily, are you OK?" he asked, worried.

Lily nodded, still sniffling. She looked at the automobile and felt sorry too. She saw a small dent and a scratch on the roof where the ball had hit.

"Uh-oh, we're in trouble!" she said, scared.

Just then, the door of the house opened and a man came out. He was wearing a suit and a tie and had a briefcase in his hand. He walked to the automobile and saw the twins and the damage.

"Hey, what are you doing here? What did you do to my automobile?" he shouted, angry.

Lily and Ben were very afraid. They didn't know what to say or do. They wished they had listened to Ben and bounced the ball somewhere else. They learned a hard lesson that day.

Lily loved to play with her doll, Rose. She hugged her, dressed her, and talked to her every day. Rose was her best friend. But one day, Lily's mom said they had to move to a new house. Lily was sad. She did not want to leave her old house and her old friends.

"Mom, can I take Rose with me?" Lily asked.

"Of course, sweetie. You can take Rose and all your other toys. Don't worry, you will make new friends in the new house," Mom said.

Lily packed Rose in a box with her other toys. She wrote "Lily's toys" on the box with a crayon. She hoped Rose would not be scared in the dark box. She kissed her goodbye and said, "I love you, Rose. I will see you soon."

The next day, they got in the car and drove to the new house. It was very far away. Lily looked out the window and saw the trees and the sky. She missed her old house and her old friends. She felt a tear roll down her cheek. She wanted to see Rose again.

When they arrived at the new house, Lily ran to find her box of toys. She opened it and looked for Rose. But she could not find her. She searched in all the other boxes, but Rose was not there. She felt a lump in her throat. She started to weep.

"Mom, where is Rose? I can't find her. She is lost," Lily cried.

Mom came and hugged Lily. She looked at the boxes and saw a label that said "Donate". She realized that Lily's box of toys had been mixed up with the box of toys they were giving away to other children.

"Oh, Lily, I'm so sorry. There was a mistake. Your box of toys was taken to the donation center. We have to go there and get it back. Maybe Rose is still there," Mom said.

Lily and Mom got in the car and drove to the donation center. It was a big building with many boxes and bags of things. Lily and Mom asked the people there if they had seen a box with Lily's toys. They said they had, but they did not know where it was. They said they had given some boxes to other places, like schools and hospitals and shelters.

Lily felt her heart sink. She wondered if Rose was in one of those places. She wondered if Rose was happy or sad. She wondered if Rose missed her. She wished she could see her again.

She looked at the distant pine trees outside the window. They reminded her of her old house and her old friends. She felt a sob in her chest. She wept.

"Give me the cord, it's mine!" Ben shouted.

"No, it's mine, I saw it first!" Lily yelled.

They pulled and pulled, but the cord did not break. It only made louder and louder sounds. The sounds were like a siren, a horn, a bell, and a whistle. They were very loud and annoying.

Mom and Dad heard the noise and came to their room. They saw Ben and Lily fighting over the cord. They were not happy.

"What are you doing?" Mom asked.

"Stop that noise!" Dad said.

They took the cord away from Ben and Lily. They looked at it and saw a tag. The tag said, "This is not a toy. This is an ordinary cord for the fire alarm. Do not pull it or you will make a false alarm."

Mom and Dad explained to Ben and Lily that the cord was not a toy, but a tool for safety. They said that pulling the cord could make the firemen come for no reason, and that was not good. They said that Ben and Lily should not fight over things, but share them nicely. They said that they had many toys that were more fun than an ordinary cord.

Ben and Lily felt sorry for what they did. They said sorry to Mom and Dad, and to each other. They hugged and said, "Let's play together with our toys."

One day, Lily sees a new bird in the garden. It is pink and pretty, and it sings a sweet song. Lily wants to make friends with the pink bird. She runs to the house and gets her birdcage. She puts some seeds and water in the cage, and then she goes back to the garden.

She sees the pink bird on a branch. She says, "Hello, pink bird. Do you want to come with me? I have a nice cage for you, and some food and water. You can be my new pet, and I will give you a name. How about Rosie?"

The pink bird looks at Lily and the cage. It thinks for a moment. It likes the seeds and the water, but it does not like the cage. It likes to fly and be free. It says, "No, thank you, Lily. I do not want to go with you. I do not want to be in a cage. I want to stay in the garden, and sing with my friends. I already have a name. It is Ruby."

Lily feels sad. She likes the pink bird, and she wants to play with it. She says, "Please, Ruby, come with me. I will be nice to you, and you will be happy in the cage. You can still sing, and I will listen to you."

Ruby shakes her head. She says, "No, Lily, I cannot come with you. I will not be happy in the cage. I will miss the sky, and the trees, and the flowers. I will miss my friends, and they will miss me. You have other pets, and they need you. You should go back to them, and leave me alone."

Lily understands. She knows that Ruby is right. She loves her pets, and they love her. She does not want to make Ruby unhappy. She says, "OK, Ruby, I will go back to them. I am sorry for bothering you. You are a beautiful bird, and I hope you have a good life. Goodbye, Ruby."

Ruby smiles. She says, "Goodbye, Lily. You are a kind girl, and I hope you have a good life, too. Thank you for the seeds and the water. Maybe I will see you again, someday."

Lily takes her cage and goes back to the house. She hugs her dog, her cat, and her bird. She tells them about Ruby, and they listen to her. She is happy with her pets, and she does not think about the pink bird anymore.

Lily wanted to find out. She ran to the button and pushed it. Nothing happened. She pushed it again and again. Still nothing.

"Maybe it's broken," she said.

Suddenly, they heard a loud siren. They saw a fire truck coming to the park. The firemen jumped out and ran to the button.

"Who pushed this?" one of them asked.

Lily and Ben were scared. They hid behind a tree.

"We did," Lily said in a small voice.

The fireman looked at them. He was not angry. He smiled.

"Don't worry, kids. This is a test button. We use it to practice for real events. It's safe. But you shouldn't push it unless there is a fire. It makes a lot of noise and it can confuse people."

Lily and Ben felt sorry. They said they were sorry.

"It's okay," the fireman said. "You didn't know. But now you do. Next time, ask an adult before you push a button you don't know. Okay?"

Lily and Ben nodded. They thanked the fireman. He gave them stickers and a hat. They were happy.

They learned a new word: event. They also learned to be careful with buttons. They went back to the swings and the slide. They had fun.

She looked at Ben and Sam. They were playing with their ball and having fun. They were still winning and scoring goals. They smiled and waved at her. They invited her to join them.

Lila felt lonely and silly. She realized that she was not independent. She needed her friends and their ball. She wanted to play and have fun with them. She wanted to share and be nice.

She picked up her ball and walked back to them. She apologized and asked if she could play with them.

"Of course you can," Ben and Sam said. "We are happy to share our ball with you. We are your friends and we want to play with you."

They gave her a hug and handed her the ball. Lila smiled and thanked them. She kicked the ball and scored a goal. They cheered and clapped for her. They played together and had a great time. Lila learned that being independent is good, but being friendly is better.

"What is that?" Lily asks.

"That is a clock. It tells the time," Tom says.

"What is time?" Lily asks.

"Time is when things happen. Like when we eat, or sleep, or play," Tom says.

"How do you know the time?" Lily asks.

"You look at the clock. The hands point to the numbers. The big hand is for minutes. The small hand is for hours," Tom says.

"Can you show me?" Lily asks.

"Sure. Come with me. I will bring my watch," Tom says.

Tom and Lily go to the clock tower. Tom shows Lily his watch. It is small and has numbers and hands too.

"See? My watch tells the same time as the clock. Look, the big hand is on six and the small hand is on three. That means it is three thirty," Tom says.

"Wow, you are very wise, Tom. You know a lot about time," Lily says.

"Thank you, Lily. You are very kind. Do you want to learn more about time?" Tom asks.

"Yes, please. I want to be wise too," Lily says.

Tom and Lily smile. They sit on a bench and watch the clock. Tom teaches Lily how to read the time. They have fun and learn something new. They are happy friends.

The brothers looked around. They saw a policeman standing near them. He had seen everything. He was not happy with Sam.

"Who are you?" Sam asked.

"I am a policeman. I am here to help the man. He was robbed and killed by bad people. They took his money and ran away. He was a good man. He worked hard to help his family and his community. He did not deserve to die," the policeman said.

He looked at Ben and smiled. "You are a good boy. You tried to stop your brother from doing something wrong. You have a good heart. You should be proud of yourself."

He looked at Sam and frowned. "You are a bad boy. You tried to take the money from the man. You did not care about his life or his family. You only cared about yourself. You have a bad heart. You should be ashamed of yourself."

He took the money from the man's hand and put it in his pocket. He said, "This money belongs to his family. I will give it to them. They need it more than you. You need to learn a lesson. You need to say sorry to the man and to your brother. You need to change your ways. You need to be like Ben, not like Sam."

Sam felt sorry. He realized he was wrong. He said, "I am sorry, Mr. Policeman. I am sorry, dead man. I am sorry, Ben. I was bad. I will be good. I will be like Ben, not like Sam."

Ben hugged Sam. He said, "I forgive you, Sam. I love you, brother. We can share our cars and balls. We can be happy and good."

The policeman nodded. He said, "That is good, boys. You have learned a valuable lesson. Money is not everything. Kindness and honesty are more important. You should always respect and help others. You should always be like Ben, not like Sam."

The end.

If he wags his tail and licks your hand, he is happy to meet you. If he growls or barks, he is scared or angry and you should leave him alone."

Lily nodded and followed her mom's advice. She walked slowly to the dog and said, "Hello, dog. My name is Lily. Can I be your friend?" She held out her hand and waited for the dog to sniff it. The dog wagged his tail and licked her hand. He was a friendly dog. Lily smiled and petted the dog gently. The dog liked Lily and licked her face.

Lily's mom was proud of her daughter. She said, "You are a smart girl, Lily. You know how to introduce yourself to a new friend. You have wisdom, unlike some foolish people who try to pet dogs without asking first. They might get bitten or hurt the dog. You are kind and respectful to animals. That is a good thing."

Lily hugged her mom and said, "Thank you, mom. I love you. And I love the dog, too. Can we come back to the park and see him again?"

Her mom said, "Of course, Lily. Maybe we can ask his owner his name and learn more about him. He seems to like you, too. Maybe he can be your new friend."

Lily was happy. She had learned something new and made a new friend. She said goodbye to the dog and waved to his owner. She hoped to see them again soon. She liked the park and all the animals there. She was a curious and wise girl.

Mia clapped and cheered. She wanted to try too. She waited for Ben to come back. But something bad happened. The branch that Ben tied the rope to was very old and weak. It broke with a loud crack. Ben fell down hard. He hit his head on a rock. He did not move or make a sound.

Mia screamed. She ran to Ben and shook him. He did not wake up. She cried and cried. She did not know what to do. She was scared and alone.

A man heard Mia's scream. He came to the park and saw Ben and Mia. He called for help. He tried to help Ben, but it was too late. Ben was gone. Mia lost her friend. She was very sad. She wished they never found the rope. She wished they never played with the old oak tree.

Ben and Lily were best friends. They liked to play in the park every day. They had a secret spot under a big tree, where they hid their toys and snacks.

One day, they found a big apple under the tree. It was red and shiny and looked very yummy. Ben and Lily decided to share it. They each took a bite and smiled.

"This is the best apple ever!" Ben said.

"Let's save some for later!" Lily said.

They wrapped the apple in a leaf and put it in their secret spot. Then they went to play on the swings.

The next day, they came back to the park. They ran to their secret spot to get the apple. But when they unwrapped the leaf, they saw something horrible. The apple was brown and soft and had holes in it. It smelled very bad.

"Yuck! What happened to our apple?" Ben asked.

"It rotted!" Lily said. "Maybe some bugs ate it."

They felt very sad and angry. They threw the apple away and stomped their feet.

"Who did this to our apple?" Ben said.

"Maybe it was Tom. He is mean and always takes our toys." Lily said.

"Let's go and tell him to leave us alone!" Ben said.

They marched to the other side of the park, where Tom was playing with his ball. They shouted at him and accused him of ruining their apple.

Tom looked confused and scared. He said he didn't know what they were talking about. He said he never touched their apple. He said he was sorry they were upset, but he didn't do anything wrong.

Ben and Lily didn't believe him. They kept yelling and calling him names. They made him cry and run away.

They felt proud and happy. They thought they had taught Tom a lesson. They went back to their secret spot and looked for another snack.

But when they got there, they saw something else. Their toys and snacks were gone. All they found was a note that said:

"Dear Ben and Lily,

I saw your apple yesterday. It looked very yummy. I wanted to have a bite, but I saw you had wrapped it in a leaf. I thought you wanted to save it for later. I was very hungry, but I didn't touch it. I was loyal to you.

But today, I saw your apple again. It was rotten and smelly. I felt sorry for you. I thought you would be sad and angry. I wanted to make you happy. I took your toys and snacks and gave them to some other kids who had nothing. I thought you would be proud and generous. I was loyal to you.

I hope you understand. I hope you forgive me. I hope you are still my friends.

Love,

Tom"

Ben and Lily read the note. They felt very ashamed and sorry. They realized they had made a big mistake. They had blamed Tom for something he didn't do. They had hurt his feelings and lost his trust. They had been mean and selfish.

They looked at each other and said:

"We were wrong. Tom was loyal to us. We were not loyal to him. We need to say sorry. We need to be his friends."

They ran to the other side of the park, where Tom was sitting on a bench. They hugged him and apologized. They thanked him for being loyal to them. They asked him to share his ball with them.

Tom smiled and forgave them. He said he was happy they were still his friends. He said he didn't mind giving away their toys and snacks. He said he had enough for everyone.

They played with the ball for a long time. They laughed and had fun. They learned a lesson. They learned to be loyal to each other.

Their dad says that they cannot buy passports. He says that passports are not for sale. He says that they have to apply for passports. He says that they need to fill out forms and take photos and pay fees.

Lily and Ben do not like this. They think that this is too hard and too boring. They want to have passports now. They have an idea. They go to their room. They take some paper and some crayons. They draw pictures of themselves. They write their names and their ages. They cut out the paper. They say that these are their passports.

They go back to their dad. They show him their passports. They say that they are ready to go to other countries. They ask him where they should go first. Their dad smiles. He says that their passports are very nice. He says that they are very creative. He says that he is proud of them. But he also says that their passports are not real. He says that they cannot use them to travel. He says that they have to wait until they are older.

Lily and Ben are sad. They do not want to wait. They want to travel now. They say that this is not fair. They say that their dad has a passport and they do not. They say that they want to play a game with their dad. They say that the game is called "Who has the best passport?". They say that the winner gets to choose where to go.

Their dad laughs. He says that this is a silly game. He says that he loves them very much. He says that he will play the game with them. He says that he will let them choose where to go. But he says that they cannot go right now. He says that they have to go in their imagination. He says that they have to pretend that they are in another country. He says that they have to tell him what they see and what they do.

Lily and Ben agree. They think that this is a fun game. They think that they can still win. They take their passports and their dad's passport. They sit on the couch. They close their eyes. They start to imagine. They start to tell their dad their stories. They start to smile. They start to have fun.

Sara and Ben had an idea. They wanted to sell the leather things and buy more toys. They asked mom and dad if they could do that. Mom and dad said yes, but they had to be careful and not talk to strangers. They gave them a table and a sign that said "Leather things for sale".

Sara and Ben set up their table in front of the house. They waited for people to come and buy their leather things. They saw a man walking by. He had a big coat and a hat and a beard. He looked at their table and smiled.

"Hello, little ones," he said. "What do you have here?"

Sara and Ben told him they had leather things for sale. They showed him their hats and belts and bags. They told him they made them by themselves.

The man nodded and said they were very beautiful and well-made. He said he wanted to buy them all. He asked them how much they wanted for them.

Sara and Ben were very happy. They said they wanted ten dollars for each thing. They thought that was a lot of money.

The man said that was a fair price. He said he had the money in his car. He asked them to come with him and help him carry the leather things. He said he would give them the money there.

Sara and Ben agreed. They thought the man was nice and honest. They followed him to his car. They did not see the sign on his car that said "Leather dealer". They did not hear him laugh as he drove away with their leather things. They did not get any money or toys. They only got sad and scared. They had made a big mistake.

Jack and Jill like to play on the beach. They make sand castles and look for shells. One day, they find a big metal thing in the sand. It is an anchor. It is very heavy and rusty.

"Wow, look at this!" Jack says. "It is an anchor. It is for boats. Let's take it home!"

"No, we can't," Jill says. "It is too big and too heavy. And it is not ours. We have to leave it here."

"But I want it!" Jack says. He is stubborn. He tries to pull the anchor out of the sand. He pulls and pulls, but it does not move.

"Jack, stop it!" Jill says. "You will hurt yourself. And you will make a mess. Come on, let's go play with something else."

"No, I want the anchor!" Jack says. He does not listen to Jill. He keeps pulling the anchor.

Jill is sad. She does not want to play with Jack anymore. She walks away and finds a nice spot to make a sand castle. She has fun with her bucket and shovel.

Jack is still pulling the anchor. He is tired and angry. He does not have fun. He looks around and sees that Jill is gone. He feels lonely.

"Jill, where are you?" he calls. "Jill, come back!"

He hears Jill's voice from far away. "I am here, Jack. I am making a sand castle. Do you want to join me?"

Jack thinks for a moment. He looks at the anchor. He looks at Jill. He decides to join Jill. He lets go of the anchor and runs to Jill.

"Jill, I am sorry," he says. "You were right. The anchor is not good. Can I play with you?"

"Of course, Jack," Jill says. "You are my friend. Here, you can help me with the sand castle."

Jack and Jill hug and smile. They play together and have fun. They forget about the anchor. They are happy.

Ben and Lily were having lunch with their mom. Mom made them some soup and bread. Ben liked soup, but Lily did not. She said soup was too hot and boring.

"Try some, Lily. It's good for you," Mom said.

"No, thank you. I want something else," Lily said.

Mom sighed. She gave Lily a sandwich with cheese and ham. Lily smiled. She liked cheese and ham. She took a big bite of her sandwich.

But something was wrong. The sandwich was not normal. It was spicy. Very spicy. Lily felt a fire in her mouth. She coughed and spit out the sandwich. She grabbed her water and drank it fast. But it did not help. The fire was still there.

Lily started to cry. She felt panic. She did not like spicy food. It hurt her mouth and nose. She wanted the fire to go away.

"Mom, Mom, help me! My sandwich is spicy! It burns!" Lily shouted.

Mom looked at Lily. She saw the red sauce on the sandwich. She realized what happened. She had used the wrong jar. She had used the spicy sauce that Dad liked, not the normal sauce that Lily liked.

"Oh, Lily, I'm so sorry. I made a mistake. Here, have some milk. It will make the fire go away," Mom said.

She gave Lily a glass of milk. Lily drank it slowly. She felt the fire go away. She felt better. She stopped crying.

"Thank you, Mom. I'm sorry I spit out the sandwich. I was scared," Lily said.

"It's okay, Lily. I'm sorry I gave you the spicy sauce. I should have checked the jar. Are you feeling better now?" Mom said.

"Yes, Mom. I'm feeling better. But I don't want any more sandwich. Can I have some soup instead?" Lily said.

Mom smiled. She was glad Lily was feeling better. She gave her some soup and bread. Lily liked the soup. It was not spicy. It was warm and yummy.

Ben watched Lily and Mom. He felt curious. He wanted to try the spicy sauce. He liked spicy food. He took a bite of Lily's sandwich.

But he did not like it. It was too spicy. Even for him. He felt a fire in his mouth. He coughed and spit out the sandwich. He grabbed his water and drank it fast. But it did not help. The fire was still there.

Ben started to cry. He felt panic. He did not like the spicy sauce. It hurt his mouth and nose. He wanted the fire to go away.

"Oh, Ben, what did you do? You ate Lily's sandwich. The one with the spicy sauce. Here, have some milk. It will make the fire go away," Mom said.

She gave Ben a glass of milk. Ben drank it slowly. He felt the fire go away. He felt better. He stopped crying.

"Thank you, Mom. I'm sorry I ate Lily's sandwich. I was curious," Ben said.

"It's okay, Ben. I'm sorry the sandwich was spicy. I should have thrown it away. Are you feeling better now?" Mom said.

"Yes, Mom. I'm feeling better. But I don't want any more sandwich. Can I have some soup instead?" Ben said.

Mom smiled. She was glad Ben was feeling better. She gave him some soup and bread. Ben liked the soup. It was not spicy. It was warm and yummy.

Mom looked at Ben and Lily. They were both eating their soup and bread. They were both happy. She felt sorry for the mistake. She felt proud of the kids. She felt love for them.

She said, "I love you, Ben and Lily. You are both brave and sweet. Next time, I will make sure to use the right sauce. The one that you both like."

Ben and Lily looked at Mom. They smiled. They said, "We love you, Mom. You are the best. The soup is delicious. Thank you for making it."

"Stop, dog, stop!" Tim shouted. "That is our ball! You broke it!"

The dog did not listen. The dog saw the bike and wanted to play with it too. The dog ran to the bike and pushed it. The bike fell and made a loud noise. Tim and Lily were more scared and more sad.

"Stop, dog, stop!" Lily cried. "That is our bike! You made it fall!"

The dog did not listen. The dog saw Tim and Lily's lunch bag and wanted to eat it too. The dog ran to the lunch bag and opened it. The lunch bag had two sandwiches and two apples. The dog ate one sandwich and one apple. The sandwich was cheese and ham and the apple was red and juicy. Tim and Lily were very scared and very sad.

"Stop, dog, stop!" Tim and Lily yelled. "That is our lunch! You ate it!"

The dog did not listen. The dog was full and happy. The dog licked his lips and wagged his tail. The dog saw the other sandwich and the other apple and wanted to eat them too. The dog reached for them with his mouth.

But then, a man came. The man was tall and brown and had a big hat. The man was the dog's owner. The man saw the dog and the mess and was angry.

"Bad dog, bad dog!" the man said. "What have you done? You ruined the kids' toys and food! You are a naughty and smelly dog!"

The man grabbed the dog by the collar and pulled him away. The man said sorry to Tim and Lily and gave them some money. The man and the dog left the park.

Tim and Lily were still scared and sad. They had no ball, no bike and no lunch. They hugged each other and cried. They wanted to go home.

Mia smiles. She is happy. She thinks she is a good racer.

"Thank you!" Mia says. "But your blue car is also fast. And it is very pretty. I like the blue color."

Tom smiles too. He is happy. He thinks Mia is a nice friend.

"Thank you!" Tom says. "Do you want to trade cars? You can play with my blue car and I can play with your red car."

"OK!" Mia says. "That sounds fun. Let's trade cars and race again."

They trade cars and race again. They have fun. They make zoom sounds and laugh. They are happy. They are friends.

Max was angry too. He said, "No, you have to share! I'm bigger than you!" He pulled on the toys and tried to get into the bathtub. He did not want to wait for Lily.

Their mom heard the noise and came to the bathroom. She saw Lily and Max fighting over the bathtub. She was not happy. She said, "Stop it, both of you! You have to learn to share and take turns. Now get out of the bath and dry yourselves. You can take a bath again tomorrow, but only if you behave."

Ben heard Lily's voice and felt scared. He was hiding behind the bush, but he knew Lily would see him soon. He wanted to run away, but he was too sleepy. One day, she found a new top in her toy box. It was black and shiny, with a silver star on it. It looked very mysterious. Anna wondered where it came from. She decided to try it out. She spun it on the floor and watched it go faster and faster. It made a strange humming sound.

"Wow, what is that?" Ben asked, pointing at the top.

"OK, how do I do it?" Ben said, taking the top from Anna.

Anna showed him how to hold the top and twist it with his fingers. "You have to spin it hard and let it go. Then it will spin on the floor. Like this." She spun another top and watched it go.

Ben nodded and tried to do the same. He spun the top hard and let it go. But something went wrong. The top flew out of his hand and hit the wall. It bounced back and hit the lamp. The lamp fell over and broke. The room went dark.

"Uh-oh," Anna said.

They heard their mom coming up the stairs. She sounded angry.

"Uh-oh," they said together.

Tim looked around the park. He saw the swings, the slide, the sandbox, and the fountain. He did not see Jen. He wondered where she was. He decided to check behind the trees. He walked to the first tree and peeked behind it. He saw nothing. He walked to the second tree and peeked behind it. He saw nothing. He walked to the third tree and peeked behind it. He saw a cloth.

"Got you!" Tim shouted and pulled the cloth. He expected to see Jen, but he saw something else. He saw a big, furry, angry raccoon. The raccoon hissed and showed its sharp teeth. Tim was scared. He dropped the cloth and ran away. He screamed for Jen.

Jen heard Tim's scream. She came out from behind the tree. She saw Tim running and the raccoon chasing him. She was scared too. She ran after Tim. She shouted for help.

A man who was walking his dog heard Jen's shout. He saw Tim and Jen running and the raccoon following them. He whistled for his dog. His dog was big and brave. His dog barked and ran to the raccoon. The raccoon stopped and turned around. The dog and the raccoon faced each other. The dog growled and the raccoon hissed.

Tim and Jen reached the man. They were trembling. They hugged the man. The man hugged them back. He asked them if they were okay. They nodded. They thanked him and his dog. The man smiled and said they were welcome. He said they should be careful when playing in the park. He said some animals might not like to be disturbed. He said they should always ask before touching a cloth.

Tim and Jen agreed. They said they were sorry. They said they learned their lesson. They said they would not touch a cloth again. They said they would rather touch a sour lemon. They laughed. The man laughed too. His dog wagged its tail. The raccoon ran away.

One day, they saw a big truck parked near the park. It had a sign that said "Gas". Lily and Tom were curious. They wanted to see what was inside the truck.

They walked closer to the truck and saw a man with a hose. He was putting gas in a car. Lily and Tom said hello to the man.

"Hello, kids. What are you doing here?" the man asked.

"We are playing with our ball. What are you doing?" Lily asked.

"I am giving gas to the car. The car needs gas to go. Do you know what gas is?" the man said.

Lily and Tom shook their heads. They did not know what gas was.

"Gas is a kind of air that you cannot see. It is in this hose and in this tank. It makes the car move. But you have to be careful. Gas can be dangerous. You should not touch it or smell it. It can hurt you," the man explained.

Lily and Tom nodded. They understood. They did not want to get hurt.

"Thank you for telling us. Can we see your truck?" Tom asked.

"Sure, you can see my truck. But you have to stay away from the hose and the tank. Come, I will show you," the man said.

He took them to the front of the truck. He opened the door and let them peek inside.

She pointed to a sticker on the dashboard. It was a picture of a cute brown dog with floppy ears.

"That is my dog. His name is Spot. He is very cute and friendly. He likes to ride with me in the truck. Do you like dogs?" the man asked.

Lily and Tom smiled. They liked dogs. They had a dog at home. His name was Rex. He was a cute black dog with a white spot on his chest.

"Yes, we like dogs. We have a dog too. His name is Rex. He is very cute and friendly too. He likes to play with us and our ball," Lily said.

"Really? That is nice. Maybe Rex and Spot can be friends. Do you want to meet Spot? He is in the back of the truck. He is sleeping now, but he will wake up soon," the man said.

Lily and Tom nodded. They wanted to meet Spot. They followed the man to the back of the truck. He opened the door and they saw a cute brown dog with floppy ears. He was lying on a blanket and snoring.

"Hello, Spot. We are Lily and Tom. We are playing in the park. We like your picture. You are very cute," Lily said.

She reached out her hand and petted the dog. The dog licked her hand and nuzzled her. Tom did the same. The dog licked his hand and nuzzled him.

"Hello, Lily and Tom. I am Spot. I am riding in the truck. I like my picture too. You are very cute too," the dog said.

He did not really say that, but Lily and Tom imagined that he did. They laughed and hugged the dog. The dog wagged his tail and licked their faces.

The next day, the bossy cat Sam asked the frog to join them for tea. The frog was very happy and said yes. Now, Sam, Max, and the frog had tea together every day. They all became good friends and had lots of fun watching the frog spring in the garden.

As they stirred the soup together, Lily felt warm and happy inside. She loved spending time with her mom in the kitchen. "This soup smells so good," Lily said. "I can't wait to eat it!" Her mom smiled and said, "Me too, Lily. Me too."

One day, they saw a new log near the pond. It was long and brown and had some green stuff on it. Anna wanted to climb on it and see what was on the other side of the pond. Ben was not sure. He thought the log looked wet and slippery.

"Come on, Ben, let's go!" Anna said. She ran to the log and jumped on it. She held her stick and pointed to the pond. "Look, there's a duck! Maybe it's a treasure duck!"

Ben followed her slowly. He put his hat on his head and tried to balance on the log. He looked at the duck. It was white and yellow and had a funny beak. He wondered if it had any gold or jewels.

Suddenly, the log moved. It was not a log at all. It was a big crocodile! It opened its mouth and showed its sharp teeth. It made a loud noise that scared Anna and Ben.

"Aaaah!" Anna and Ben screamed. They dropped their stick and hat and jumped off the crocodile. They ran back to the shore and hid behind a tree. They were wet and muddy and embarrassed.

The duck laughed. It was not a treasure duck. It was a trick duck. It had put the crocodile there to fool Anna and Ben. It thought it was very funny.

"Ha ha ha!" The duck said. "You thought it was a log, but it was a croc! You are silly pirates, and I am a clever duck!"

Anna and Ben did not like the duck. They did not like the crocodile. They did not like the pond. They decided to play somewhere else. They never climbed on logs again.

One day, Sara wanted to play castle, but Tom wanted to play spaceship. They disagreed and started to argue.

"I want to be the princess and you be the knight!" Sara said.

"No, I want to be the astronaut and you be the alien!" Tom said.

They both pulled and pushed the armchair, trying to get on it. They did not listen to each other or share. They were not cheerful, they were angry and rude.

Their mom heard the noise and came to the living room. She saw the twins fighting over the armchair and was very upset.

"What are you doing?" she asked. "Why are you not playing nicely?"

Sara and Tom stopped and looked at their mom. They felt ashamed and sorry.

"We wanted to play different things and we disagreed," Sara said.

"We both wanted the armchair and we did not want to take turns," Tom said.

Their mom shook her head and said, "That is not how you treat each other or your toys. You should respect each other's choices and learn to compromise. And you should be careful with the armchair, it is not a toy, it is a furniture. You could break it or hurt yourself."

She took the twins by the hand and led them to their room. She said, "You are not allowed to play with the armchair anymore. You have to stay in your room and think about what you did. Maybe you can write a sorry note to each other and to the armchair."

They wrote their sorry notes and hugged each other. They hoped their mom would forgive them and let them play with the armchair again. But they did not know that the armchair was already broken and had to be thrown away. They had lost their favorite toy because of their selfishness and carelessness.

The moral of the story is: Be kind and respectful to others, even when you disagree. And take good care of your things, or you might lose them.

Sara and Ben were twins who liked to play outside. One day, they found a big gray rock in the garden. They wanted to see what was inside the rock, so they tried to break it with a stick. But the rock was too hard and the stick broke.

"Let's ask Mom for help," Sara said. "Maybe she has a tool to open the rock."

"OK," Ben agreed. They ran inside the house and looked for Mom. They found her in the kitchen, making a cake.

"Mom, Mom, can you help us?" Sara asked. "We found a gray rock and we want to see what's inside."

Mom smiled and put down the bowl. "Sure, I can help you. But first, you have to wash your hands. You are very dirty from playing outside."

Sara and Ben washed their hands and followed Mom to the garden. Mom brought a hammer and a chisel. She put the rock on the ground and tapped it with the chisel. The rock cracked and split in two.

"Wow!" Sara and Ben exclaimed. They looked inside the rock and saw something shiny and colorful. It was a geode, a rock with crystals inside.

"What is this?" Ben asked.

"It's a geode, a special kind of rock that has crystals inside. They are formed when water and minerals fill the holes in the rock and harden over time. They are very beautiful and rare," Mom explained.

"Can we keep it?" Sara asked.

"Of course, you can. It's your lucky find. But you have to share it with each other, OK?" Mom said.

"OK," Sara and Ben said. They hugged Mom and thanked her for helping them. They took the geode inside and put it on their shelf. They admired the sparkling crystals and felt happy.

Mom went back to the kitchen and finished the cake. She cut a big slice for Sara and Ben and put a strawberry on top. She called them to come and eat.

"Sara, Ben, come and have some cake. It's yummy and has a strawberry on top," Mom said.

Sara and Ben ran to the kitchen and saw the cake. They smiled and sat down. They picked up their forks and were about to eat, when they noticed something.

"Mom, the strawberry is melting!" Sara said.

"Melting?" Mom asked. She looked at the strawberry and saw that it was dripping red juice. She realized what happened. She had put the strawberry in the freezer to keep it fresh, but she forgot to take it out before putting it on the cake. The strawberry was frozen and now it was thawing.

"Oh, I'm sorry, sweeties. I made a mistake. I put the strawberry in the freezer and it became hard and cold. Now it's becoming soft and warm again. That's what melting means," Mom said.

"Can we still eat it?" Ben asked.

"Sure, you can. It's still a strawberry, just a different shape. It might taste a little different, but it's still good for you," Mom said.

Sara and Ben shrugged and ate the cake and the strawberry. They liked it anyway. They learned a new word and a new thing. They thanked Mom for the cake and gave her a kiss.

The moral of the story is: Sometimes things change shape or form, but they are still the same inside. We can learn from our mistakes and try new things. We should share our discoveries and joys with others.

Suddenly, they heard a noise. They both stopped and peeked over a bush to see what it was. It was a bird with a broken wing. Lily and Jack forgot about the diamond and decided to help the bird instead. They worked together to make a little nest for the bird and gave it some food and water.

In the end, Lily and Jack realized that helping others was more important than having a diamond. They became friends and played together every day in the park, always keeping an eye out for any animals that needed their help.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in her big backyard. One day, she saw an orange hanging from a tree. It looked juicy and delicious!

Lily wanted to pick the orange, but it was too high up. She tried to climb the tree, but she was too small. She asked her dad for help, but he was busy.

Later that day, Lily was playing with her ball when she heard a loud noise. She looked up and saw the orange had fallen from the tree! It was impressive how it had fallen all the way down. Lily was so happy, she picked up the orange and ate it right away. It was the best orange she had ever tasted!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a friendly dog named Max. Max was always by her side, and they loved to play together. One day, Lily and Max went for a walk in the woods. They were having so much fun until the sky started to get dark, and they got lost.

Lily said, "Max, we need to find our way back home. Let's search for a light." Max barked in agreement, and they started to look around. Suddenly, they saw a light in the distance. They ran towards it, hoping it would lead them home.

When they got closer, they saw that it was a friendly old man with a lantern. He asked them what they were doing out so late, and they told him they were lost. The old man smiled and said he would help them find their way back home.

Thanks to the kind old man and his lantern, Lily and Max made it back home safe and sound. From that day on, they always made sure to stay on the path and never wander off again.

Once upon a time, there was a farmer who had a big farm with many animals. He had cows, pigs, chickens, and sheep. One day, he asked his little daughter to count all the animals on the farm. She counted all the cows, pigs, chickens, and sheep and told her father the number.

But then, the farmer realized that he forgot to feed the chickens. He felt embarrassed because the chickens were hungry. He quickly went to the chicken coop and gave them some food. After that, the little girl counted the chickens again and they were all happy and full. The end.

Lily and Ben are friends. They like to play with toys and books. They also like to listen to music. Music makes them happy and calm.

One day, Lily and Ben go to the park with their moms. They see a man playing a guitar. He has a hat on the ground. People put money in the hat. The man sings songs and smiles.

"Look, he has music!" Lily says to Ben.

"Yes, he does. He is good at music," Ben says.

"Do you think he is wealthy?" Lily asks.

"What is wealthy?" Ben says.

"Wealthy means you have a lot of money and things," Lily says.

"Oh. I don't know. Maybe he is, maybe he isn't," Ben says.

Lily and Ben walk closer to the man. They like his music. They clap their hands and dance.

The man sees them and stops playing. He says, "Hello, little ones. Do you like my music?"

"Yes, we do!" Lily and Ben say.

"Thank you. You are very kind. Do you want to try my guitar?" the man says.

"Really? Can we?" Lily and Ben say.

"Sure. Here you go. Be careful, it is precious to me," the man says. He gives them his guitar.

Lily and Ben take turns playing the guitar. They make funny sounds and laugh. The man laughs too. He helps them hold the guitar and strum the strings.

Lily and Ben have fun with the guitar. They thank the man and give him a hug. They also give him some of their snack. The man thanks them and gives them a sticker.

Lily and Ben go back to their moms. They show them the sticker and tell them about the man.

"He was nice. He shared his music with us," Lily says.

"He was nice. He cared about us," Ben says.

Their moms smile and hug them. They say, "We are proud of you. You are nice too. You shared your snack and your love with him."

Lily and Ben smile. They feel happy. They think music is wonderful. They think caring is wonderful. They think they are wealthy.

Tommy loved to sail with his daddy. They had a small boat that was blue and white. It had a big sail that caught the wind and made the boat go fast. Tommy liked to sit in the front and watch the water and the birds.

One day, they sailed to a small island. There were many trees and flowers on the island. Tommy and his daddy got off the boat and went to explore. They saw a big rock that looked like a turtle. They saw a small cave that had shiny stones inside. They saw a friendly dog that wagged its tail and licked their faces.

"Can we stay here, daddy?" Tommy asked. "I like this island. It is fun and pretty."

Daddy smiled and hugged Tommy. "This island is nice, but we can't stay here. We have to go back to our home. Our home is where we belong. It has our bed, our toys, our books, and our mommy. Mommy is waiting for us. She made us a yummy dinner. Don't you miss mommy?"

Tommy nodded. He loved his mommy. He wanted to see her and hug her and tell her about the island. He also wanted to eat the yummy dinner. He was hungry after sailing and exploring.

"OK, daddy. Let's go back to our home. But can we come back to this island another day?"

"Sure, Tommy. We can come back to this island another day. It is our special place. But we also have our regular place. And our regular place is where our family is. And our family is the best thing in the world."

Tommy agreed. He climbed back on the boat with his daddy. They raised the sail and caught the wind. They waved goodbye to the island, the rock, the cave, and the dog. They sailed back to their home, where mommy was waiting for them. They were happy.

"Yes, please. I like fruit. What fruit do you have?" Ben asks.

"I have apples, bananas and grapes. You can choose what you want," Anna's mom says.

"I want an apple, please," Ben says.

"I want a banana, please," Anna says.

Anna's mom gives them the fruit. They peel and eat them. They are happy and full. They thank Anna's mom again. Then they go back to play. They have a lot of fun. They are good friends.

Tim and Lily were playing in the park. They saw a big pond with ducks and fish. Tim wanted to feed the ducks. He had some bread in his pocket. He ran to the edge of the pond and threw some bread into the water.

"Look, Lily, the ducks are eating the bread!" he shouted.

Lily followed him. She liked the ducks too. But she was fearful of the water. She thought the water was deep and cold. She stayed behind Tim and held his hand.

"Can I feed the ducks too?" she asked.

"Sure, here, take some bread," Tim said. He gave her some bread and smiled.

Lily took the bread. She wanted to be brave like Tim. She stepped closer to the water. She threw the bread with her other hand. But she threw it too hard. The bread flew over the water and landed on the other side.

"Oh no!" Lily said.

She let go of Tim's hand. She stepped forward to get the bread. But she did not see the rock in front of her. She tripped over the rock and fell into the water.

"Help!" she screamed.

Tim heard her scream. He turned around and saw her in the water. He was scared too. But he loved his sister. He stepped into the water and grabbed her arm. He pulled her out of the water and hugged her.

"It's okay, Lily, I got you," he said.

Lily was wet and cold. She was crying. She hugged Tim back.

"Thank you, Tim, you saved me," she said.

They walked back to the shore. They saw their mom and dad. They ran to them and told them what happened.

Mom and dad were worried. They checked if they were hurt. They were not hurt. They were just wet. Mom and dad gave them towels and warm hugs. They praised Tim for being brave and kind. They comforted Lily for being scared and sorry.

They all went home. They changed their clothes and had some hot chocolate. They cuddled on the couch and watched a movie. They were happy and safe. They loved each other.

One day, they saw a big tube in the park. It was red and shiny. Sam wanted to go inside the tube. He asked his dad, "Can we go in the tube, please?"

His dad said, "No, Sam. The tube is not for us. It is for the workers. They are fixing something under the ground. The tube is dangerous. We have to stay away from it."

Sam was curious and sad. He wanted to see what was in the tube. He thought it would be fun and exciting. He did not listen to his dad. He waited until his dad was talking to a friend. Then he ran to the tube and crawled inside.

The tube was dark and cold. Sam could not see anything. He heard loud noises and voices. He felt scared and lonely. He wanted his dad. He cried, "Dad, dad, where are you?"

His dad heard his cry. He ran to the tube and looked inside. He saw Sam's shoes and hat. He was angry and worried. He shouted, "Sam, what are you doing in there? Come out right now!"

One night, Tom heard a noise outside his window. He saw a big shadow. It was a raccoon. It wanted to eat his firefly. Tom was scared. He grabbed his jar and ran to his bed. He hugged his firefly and whispered, "Don't worry, I will protect you. You are my loyal friend."

The raccoon climbed on the window sill. It saw the jar. It reached its paw to grab it. But the firefly had a plan. It glowed very bright. It flashed its light in the raccoon's eyes. The raccoon was startled. It blinked and backed away. It fell off the window sill and ran away.
