Sara and Ben were playing in the park. They saw a big tree with many green leaves. They wanted to climb the tree and see what was up there.

"Look, Ben, there are acorns on the tree!" Sara said. "Do you think we can get them?"

"Let's try!" Ben said. "Maybe we can make a necklace with them."

They climbed the tree carefully, holding on to the branches. They reached a spot where they saw some acorns hanging. They stretched their arms to grab them.

Suddenly, they heard a loud noise. It was an enormous bird with brown feathers and a sharp beak. It was flying towards them. It wanted the acorns too.

"Watch out, Sara, it's a hawk!" Ben shouted. "It might hurt us!"

Sara and Ben were scared. They let go of the acorns and quickly climbed down the tree. They ran to their mom, who was sitting on a bench.

"Mom, mom, there was a big bird that tried to take our acorns!" Sara said.

"Are you okay, my sweeties?" Mom asked. "That was a hawk. It likes to eat acorns and sometimes small animals. You have to be careful when you play near its nest."

"We are okay, mom," Ben said. "But we didn't get any acorns."

"That's okay, Ben," Mom said. "You can find other things to play with. How about we go to the pond and feed the ducks?"

Sara and Ben nodded. They forgot about the hawk and the acorns. They followed their mom to the pond, where they saw many ducks swimming and quacking. They threw some bread crumbs to them and watched them eat. They had fun and learned something new.

Tom was a lawyer who helped people with problems. He was loyal to his friends and always told the truth. One day, he had to go to a big building where he met another lawyer who was mean and lied a lot.

The mean lawyer said, "Tom, you are wrong and I am right. You should give up and let me win. If you don't, I will pull your hair and make you cry."

Tom was not scared of the mean lawyer. He said, "No, you are wrong and I am right. You should not lie and be mean. If you do, you will have no friends and be sad."

The mean lawyer was angry and tried to pull Tom's hair. But Tom was strong and smart. He dodged the mean lawyer and said, "Stop it! You are hurting me and yourself. You should be nice and honest. Then you will have friends and be happy."

The mean lawyer realized that Tom was right. He felt sorry and said, "I'm sorry, Tom. You are a good lawyer and a good friend. I was wrong and I am sorry. Can you forgive me and be my friend?"

Tom was kind and said, "Yes, I forgive you and I can be your friend. But you have to promise to be nice and honest from now on. Then we can help people with problems together."

The mean lawyer nodded and said, "I promise, Tom. Thank you for being loyal and brave. You taught me a lesson today."

Tom smiled and said, "You're welcome. I'm glad we are friends now."

The moral of the story is: Be loyal, honest and kind, and you will have good friends and be happy. Don't be mean, lie and pull hair, or you will have no friends and be sad.

Lily caught up with Sam and saw what he did. She felt a pain in her heart. She loved Rose and did not want her to be sour. She tried to take Rose from Sam, but he was stronger. They both pulled and pushed. They struggled for Rose.

Mom heard the noise and came to the kitchen. She saw Lily and Sam fighting over the doll. She was not happy. She took Rose from Sam and gave her to Lily. She scolded Sam and said, "That was very mean, Sam. You should not hurt your sister or her doll. Say you are sorry."

Sam felt bad. He saw Lily's tears and Rose's sour face. He knew he was wrong. He said, "I'm sorry, Lily. I was just joking. I didn't mean to make you sad."

Lily looked at Sam and saw that he was sorry. She felt a little better. She said, "It's okay, Sam. I forgive you. But please don't do that again."

Mom smiled and said, "That's good, Lily. You are very kind. Now let's wash Rose and make her clean and happy again."

Lily nodded and hugged Rose. She said, "I love you, Rose. You are my best doll."

"Look, Lily, I can make my car reverse!" Tom said, pushing his car backwards with his hand.

"What does reverse mean?" Lily asked, tilting her head.

"It means go the other way. See, like this." Tom showed her how his car could go forward and backward.

"Wow, that's cool! Can I try?" Lily said, reaching for his car.

"Okay, but be careful. It's my favorite car. It's shiny and red and has a penny inside." Tom said, handing her his car.

"A penny? Why do you have a penny inside?" Lily asked, looking at the small coin in the car's window.

"It's my lucky penny. My mom gave it to me. She said it brings good luck." Tom said, smiling.

Lily nodded and held the car in her hands. She tried to make it reverse, but she pushed too hard and the car flew out of her hands. It hit the wall and broke into pieces. The penny rolled out and bounced under the sofa.

"Oh no! I'm sorry, Tom! I broke your car and your lucky penny!" Lily cried, feeling bad.

Tom ran to the broken car and picked up the pieces. He looked sad and angry.

"Lily, you're so clumsy! You ruined my car and my luck! How could you?" Tom yelled, throwing the pieces on the floor.

Lily felt tears in her eyes. She didn't mean to break his car. She wanted to say sorry, but Tom didn't want to listen. He turned away from her and crossed his arms.

Lily wished she could reverse what happened. She wished she could make everything normal again. She wished Tom would forgive her and be her friend again. She looked under the sofa and saw the penny shining. She crawled under and grabbed it. She held it in her hand and made a wish.

"Please, please, please, make Tom happy again. Make his car fix itself. Make him like me again. Please, please, please." She whispered, closing her eyes.

She opened her eyes and saw Tom looking at her. He had a smile on his face. He held his car in his hand. It was shiny and red and had the penny inside. It was not broken anymore.

"Lily, look! My car is okay! It's like magic! And look, my lucky penny is still here! It must have worked!" Tom said, showing her his car.

Lily couldn't believe it. She smiled and hugged him.

"I'm sorry, Tom. I didn't mean to break your car. I'm glad it's okay. And I'm glad you're okay." She said, feeling happy.

"Really? Can we share it?" Lily asked, feeling lucky.

"Sure, we can share it. We can share everything. We can share our cars, and our toys, and our games. And we can make them reverse together." Tom said, feeling friendly.

"Yay! That sounds fun! Let's play!" Lily said, feeling excited.

Lily liked to play in the garden. She liked to look at the flowers and the bugs. One day, she saw a caterpillar on a leaf. It was green and fuzzy. Lily wanted to touch it.

She reached out her hand and picked up the caterpillar. It tickled her fingers. She smiled and put it in her pocket. She wanted to show it to her mom and dad.

She ran to the house and looked for them. She found them in the kitchen. They were making lunch. Lily said, "Look what I have!" She took out the caterpillar from her pocket.

Mom and dad looked at the caterpillar. They looked at Lily. They looked angry. Mom said, "Lily, where did you get that?"

Lily said, "I found it in the garden. It is my friend."

Dad said, "Lily, that is not your friend. That is a caterpillar. It belongs in the garden. It needs to eat leaves and make a cocoon. You can't keep it in your pocket. You have to give it back."

Lily felt sad. She liked the caterpillar. She didn't want to give it back. She said, "But I like it. Can I keep it? Please?"

Mom said, "No, Lily. You can't keep it. It is not fair to the caterpillar. It is not a toy. It is a living thing. You have to be kind to it. You have to lend it back to the garden."

Lily felt ashamed. She knew mom and dad were right. She had been selfish. She had not been kind. She said, "I'm sorry, mom and dad. I'm sorry, caterpillar. I will lend you back to the garden. I hope you will be happy."

She took the caterpillar and ran back to the garden. She found the leaf where she had picked it up. She put the caterpillar on the leaf. She said, "Goodbye, caterpillar. Thank you for letting me hold you. I hope you will make a beautiful butterfly."

The caterpillar wiggled on the leaf. It seemed to say, "Thank you, Lily. You are a good girl. Goodbye."

Lily felt better. She had done the right thing. She had learned a lesson. She went back to the house and hugged mom and dad. They hugged her back. They said, "We love you, Lily. You are a good girl."

"Wow, that's a great hole, Sam! Can I help you?" Tim asked, as he ran over with his spade.

"Sure, Tim, we can make it bigger and deeper!" Sam said, as he moved over to make room for his brother.

They worked hard with their spades, digging and digging, until they had a hole that was as big as they were. They were very proud of their hole and decided to sit inside it and rest.

They gazed at the sky and saw the fluffy clouds and the bright sun. They felt the warm sand on their skin and the cool breeze on their hair. They smiled at each other and hugged.

"This is the best hole ever, Tim!" Sam said, as he squeezed his brother tight.

"I agree, Sam, this is the best hole ever!" Tim said, as he squeezed his brother back.

They stayed in their hole for a long time, enjoying their sand adventure, until their mom called them for lunch. They climbed out of their hole and ran to their mom, holding their spades and their hands. They were happy and hungry. They had a lot of fun in the sand.

One day, he decides to draw a chicken. He finds a yellow crayon and a red crayon. He looks at the book and starts to draw. He makes a round body, two legs, a beak, and a comb. He is very happy with his chicken. He shows it to his mom.

"Look, mom, I drew a chicken!" he says.

Mom smiles and hugs him. "That's a very nice chicken, Tommy. You did a great job. I'm very proud of you."

Tommy feels happy and warm. He wants to show his chicken to his dad, too. He runs to the living room, where dad is reading a newspaper. He holds up his chicken and says, "Look, dad, I drew a chicken!"

Dad looks at the chicken and frowns. He shakes his head. "That's not a chicken, Tommy. That's a duck. Chickens have wings and feathers, not just a comb. You need to draw better."

Tommy feels sad and hurt. He doesn't understand why dad is not proud of him. He thinks his chicken is good. He runs back to his mom and cries. He shows her his chicken and says, "Dad says this is not a chicken. He says this is a duck. He says I need to draw better. Is he right, mom?"

Mom hugs him and wipes his tears. She looks at his chicken and says, "Tommy, your chicken is very good. You used the right colors and shapes. You drew what you saw in the book. I'm very proud of you."

Tommy smiles and hugs her back. He feels happy and warm again. He decides to keep his chicken and hang it on the fridge. He thinks his chicken is the best chicken in the world. He is very proud of his chicken.

The elevator door opened and the man said, "Have fun at the zoo, kids. And enjoy your new friend."

He winked and left the elevator. Lily and Ben hugged the cage and ran to their mom, who was waiting for them outside.

They didn't know that they had done something bad. They only knew that they had a new friend and that they were eager to go to the zoo.

Lily and Tom were twins who liked to play with their toy cars. They had many cars of different colors and sizes, but their favorite was the big red bus. The bus had a driver who could move his head and say "beep beep" when they pressed a button.

One day, Lily and Tom were playing with the bus on the floor, when Lily had an idea. She wanted to see what was inside the driver's head. She took a pencil and tried to poke the driver's eye.

"Ow! That hurts!" the driver said. "Stop poking me!"

Tom saw what Lily was doing and got angry. He grabbed the pencil from her and said, "Lily, that's not nice! You shouldn't poke the driver. He is our friend. He helps us have fun with the bus. How would you like it if I poked your eye?"

Lily felt sorry and said, "I'm sorry, Tom. I'm sorry, driver. I was just curious. I wanted to know how he can talk and move. He is very intelligent."

Tom said, "I know, Lily. He is very intelligent. But he is also sensitive. He can feel pain and emotions. You should be gentle and respectful with him. He is not a toy. He is a living being."

Lily nodded and said, "You're right, Tom. I learned my lesson. I will never poke the driver again. I will be his friend and take good care of him."

The driver smiled and said, "Thank you, Lily. Thank you, Tom. You are very kind and smart. I'm happy to be your friend and play with you. Beep beep!"

The end.

Moral value: The story teaches the value of empathy, respect, and curiosity. It shows that poking someone can hurt them and that living beings deserve care and friendship. It also shows that being curious is good, but not at the expense of others.

Tom felt silly and sad. He wanted to cry. He looked at the clown and said, "I'm sorry. I wanted some cake. I didn't mean to slip."

The clown came to him and helped him up. He wiped his face and said, "It's okay, Tom. It was an easy mistake. Everyone slips sometimes. Even I do. Look at my shoes. They are too big for me. That's why I slip a lot. But I don't cry. I laugh. Because slipping can be funny too. Do you want to laugh with me?"

Tom looked at the clown's shoes. They were very big and funny. He looked at his own face. It was covered in cake and cream. He looked at Lily. She was smiling and holding her balloon. He felt better. He nodded and said, "Yes, I want to laugh with you."

The clown and Tom laughed together. They hugged and said, "You are a good clown. You are a good flyer. You are a good friend."

The hurricane came but the old man had been prepared. The wind was very strong, but his boat stayed safe. He was glad he had taken the time to polish his boat.

This story shows that when you work hard, you can be prepared for even difficult times. Preparation and hard work can help us to be ready for anything!

Later, Mia and her friends played with the powder. They made beautiful art on the ground. They had so much fun. When they were done, Mia put the rest of the powder back in the jar. She was happy to have a new treasure in her organized box.

Once upon a time, there was a soft bunny named Bobo. Bobo loved to play with his friends in the green grass. They would hop and jump all day long. Bobo was very good at making his friends laugh. He liked to tell them silly jokes. One day, Bobo told a joke about a big, round ball that was so light it could not weigh anything.

Bobo's friends laughed and laughed at the joke. They thought it was very funny. They wanted to find a ball like the one in the joke. So, they all went on a big adventure to look for the ball. They looked under the trees, in the bushes, and even in the soft, squishy mud.

Finally, they found a ball that was big and round, just like the one in the joke. They tried to weigh it, but it was so light that it floated away. Bobo and his friends chased after the ball, laughing and hopping all the way. They had so much fun playing with the ball that they forgot all about the joke. And they all lived happily ever after.

One day, a tiny bird came to the river to wash. The mushroom said, "Hello bird, do you need help to wash?" The bird replied, "Yes, please. Thank you, polite mushroom."

The mushroom helped the bird wash in the river. They splashed and played in the water. The bird was happy and clean. The mushroom and the bird became good friends. They played together every day.

But then, they started to argue. Tom said, "My car's face is funnier!" Sam said, "No, mine is!" They couldn't decide which car had the funniest face. So, they asked their mom to help.

Mom looked at both cars and said, "I think both cars have funny faces. You both did a great job!" Tom and Sam smiled and stopped arguing. They played with their cars and had lots of fun together.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim loved to pretend he was a judge. He would sit on a high chair and make decisions all day long.

One day, Tim's friend, Sally, came over to play. Sally brought her toy cat and dog. Tim said, "I will pretend to be a judge and help your cat and dog."

Sally said, "Okay, Tim. My cat wants to climb a high tree, but my dog wants to play with the cat. What should they do?"

Tim thought for a moment and then said, "The cat can climb the tree, but only for a little while. Then, the cat must come down and play with the dog."

Sally smiled and said, "Thank you, Judge Tim. My cat and dog will be happy now." They both laughed and continued to play pretend together.

Tommy smiled and said, "Thanks, Timmy! Do you want to play catch with my new baseball?"

Timmy nodded excitedly and the two boys played catch until the sun went down. As they walked home, Timmy put his ball back in his pocket and said, "Today was so much fun! Let's play again tomorrow!"

One day, a little girl named Lily went for a walk in the woods. She saw a big oak tree and decided to sit under it. The sun was shining and it was warm outside. She took out a book and started to read.

Suddenly, she heard a noise. It was a squirrel! The squirrel said, "This is my tree. You can't sit here!" Lily replied, "But I just want to read my book in the shade." The squirrel said, "No, this is my home. You have to leave!"

Lily didn't know what to do. She really wanted to stay and read her book, but the squirrel was not happy. Then, Lily had an idea. She said, "If you let me stay, I'll read you a story." The squirrel thought for a moment and then said, "Okay, but it better be a good story!"

So, Lily read the squirrel a story about a warm and cozy house. The squirrel loved the story and let Lily stay under the oak tree to read as long as she wanted. From that day on, they became good friends and shared the shade of the oak tree together.

Her parents saw how sad she was and decided to help. Together they were able to move the log. Jane sat on it and began to enjoy the view. But then, she saw something bad in the river. There were lots of fish, but they all had nasty black spots on them. Jane was so sad and sighed again.

But then suddenly, something strange happened. Out of the water, a friendly dolphin jumped and started playing with Jane. She laughed and smiled, no longer feeling sad. The dolphin swam away after a while, and Jane felt better. She said goodbye and thanked the dolphin for making her day so much better.

Jane climbed off the log and ran back home. From then on, she would go back often to sit on the log to look out at the river. But no matter how bad things looked, she knew the dolphin would always be there, ready to make her day brighter.

The tiny frog quickly hopped away on the road, but it was now too small to explore like it used to. It looked back at the sourberry with a sad look, hoping to become big again.

The frog was very lucky though. Not far away, it spotted a sweet berry. Without hesitating, it hopped over and ate the berry. Immediately, the frog started to grow back its normal size. It had learned its lesson!

The small frog was very happy to be the size it was before and it hopped away, never stopping to look at a sourberry ever again.

As he zips around, the shiny medal still sits around his neck. It's a reminder of his hard-earned victory.

"No, it's mine!" Ben said. "I saw it first!"

Lily and Ben were friends who liked to play in the park. One day, they saw a big slide that looked very fun. Lily wanted to try it, but Ben was scared. He said, "No, no, it is too high and too fast. I do not want to go."

Lily said, "Come on, Ben, do not be afraid. It is not so bad. We can go together. See, there is a line of other kids who want to go too. They are not scared."

Ben looked at the line and saw some kids who were smiling and some who were crying. He felt a tremble in his legs and his tummy. He said, "No, Lily, I do not want to go. You can go by yourself. I will wait here."

Lily was sad, but she did not want to force Ben. She said, "Okay, Ben, I will go by yourself. But you are missing out on the fun. I will be back soon." She joined the line and waited for her turn.

When it was her turn, she climbed up the stairs and sat on the slide. She felt a rush of excitement and joy as she slid down. She laughed and shouted, "Whee! This is so fun!" She landed on the soft grass and ran back to Ben.

Ben saw her happy face and felt a sour feeling in his heart. He wished he had gone with her. He said, "Lily, you look like you had a lot of fun. Was it scary?"

Lily said, "No, Ben, it was not scary. It was fun. You should try it too. It is not too late. Come on, let's go together. I will hold your hand."

Ben looked at the slide again and felt a tremble in his legs and his tummy. But he also felt a spark of courage in his chest. He said, "Okay, Lily, I will try it. But you have to hold my hand."

Lily smiled and said, "Of course, Ben, I will hold your hand. You are my friend. We can do this together." She took his hand and led him to the line. They landed on the soft grass and hugged each other.

Ben said, "Lily, you were right. It was not so bad. It was fun. Thank you for helping me. I am sorry I was afraid."

Lily said, "Ben, you are welcome. I am proud of you. You were brave. It is okay to be afraid sometimes. But it is better to try new things and have fun. That is how we learn and grow."

The moral of the story is: It is okay to be afraid sometimes, but it is better to try new things and have fun. That is how we learn and grow.

Lila and Max were playing in the kitchen. They liked to pretend they were chefs and make yummy food. They found an avocado on the counter and decided to use it for their salad.

"Look, Max, this is an avocado. It is green and soft and good for you," Lila said, holding the fruit in her hand.

"I don't like avocado. It is yucky and mushy and bad for me," Max said, making a face.

Lila frowned. She wanted Max to try the avocado and like it. She thought of a way to make it fun.

"Let's play a game, Max. I will cut the avocado in half and you can kick the seed. The seed is the big brown ball inside the avocado. It is hard and round and fun to kick. Maybe you will like avocado after you kick the seed," Lila said, smiling.

Max thought for a moment. He liked to kick things. He liked balls. Maybe he would like the seed.

"OK, Lila, let's play. But only if I can kick the seed first," Max said, nodding.

Lila agreed. She took a knife and cut the avocado in half. She gave one half to Max and kept the other half for herself. She put the seed on the floor and told Max to kick it.

Max ran to the seed and kicked it with his foot. The seed flew across the room and hit the wall. Max laughed. He liked to kick the seed. It was fun.

Lila clapped. She was happy that Max liked the game. She hoped he would like the avocado too.

"Good job, Max. You kicked the seed very far. Now, do you want to try the avocado? It is very tasty. You can put some salt and lemon on it and eat it with a spoon. It is like a green pudding," Lila said, holding her half of the avocado.

Max looked at the avocado. He was curious. He liked pudding. He liked salt and lemon. Maybe he would like the avocado.

"OK, Lila, I will try the avocado. But only if you try the seed. Maybe you will like the seed too. It is like a brown ball," Max said, giving his half of the avocado to Lila.

Lila laughed. She knew the seed was not good to eat. But she wanted to be nice to Max. She took the seed and pretended to bite it.

"Yum, yum, yum. The seed is very crunchy. Thank you, Max. You are a good chef," Lila said, making a funny face.

Max smiled. He was glad that Lila liked the seed. He took a spoon and scooped some avocado. He put some salt and lemon on it and tasted it.

"Mmm, mmm, mmm. The avocado is very creamy. Thank you, Lila. You are a good chef too," Max said, making a happy face.

Lila and Max hugged. They were proud of their salad. They ate the avocado and kicked the seed. They had fun.

Suddenly, Tristan stepped into a large clearing in the middle of the woods. Lying in the very centre of the clearing was another young tiger! Tristan was amazed and wasn't sure what to do. The tiger in the clearing just looked at Tristan and smiled. 

Tristan was overjoyed. He had finally found another tiger and now he could have an adventure with someone else! He said "hello" to the tiger and they decided to spend the day playing and exploring the forest together. They had a lot of fun and Tristan's adventure was even better than he had hoped.

Once there was a bull. He was very happy. He ran and ate grass in the sunny fields.

One day, the bull saw something bouncing. He ran over and found a tiny bug. The bug was very small, but it was a big surprise to the bull. Besides, the bug was so cute! 

The bull was curious. He leaned in closer, but the bug suddenly bit him! 

The bull jumped back, grumbling. He didn't like it when the bug bit him. But then he realized the bug was just being silly and friendly. The bull thought it was funny. 

So, the bull and the bug became friends. They played in the fields together. The bull was very happy to have a new friend.

Once upon a time, there were two friends. They were both very good at playing chess. Every day, they would sit and play chess together. One day, they began to fight over who was playing better.

The friends were feeling very uncomfortable. They did not want to fight anymore, so they decided to sit and think about it. They realized that instead of fighting, they could use their chess match to have fun and the winner could be happy without making the other friend feel sad.

So, the friends decided to just be nice to each other. They enjoyed their game of chess and cheered each other on when they each won. They even shared their pieces of cake they had brought to celebrate!

The moral of this story is that it can be more fun when two friends work together, rather than fight.

He decided to roll it down a hill. As he rolled it, it went faster and faster. All of a sudden, it rolled into the street. Tim was scared and he ran to get it, but it was too late. The point had already been run over by a car! Tim was sad and started to cry. Fortunately, his mom saw what happened and rushed to help him. She comforted him and gave him a hug. Then, she helped him look for another point. Thankfully, they were able to find one that was just as interesting!

Once upon a time there was a naughty little bear who loved to play all day. One day, he was feeling so tired that he yawned a big yawn. "Why are you so tired, silly bear?" asked his friend Rabbit.

The naughty little bear replied, "I stayed up late last night playing and now I am too tired." Rabbit said, "That was not a good idea! You should get some sleep."

The naughty little bear nodded his head and said, "I know! I will try to go to bed early tonight." He then yawned one more big yawn and said, "I think I should go take a nap now."

The end.

So, the child decided to lie down on the ground and stretch their arm up as far as they could. But still, they could not reach it. The child was sad because they could not get the rose.

But then the child had a great idea! The child found a stick on the ground, which they used to reach the rose. The rose was too big for their hand, so the child carefully pulled the stick towards them.

The child lay on the ground and looked at the beautiful large rose in their hand. They were so happy that their clever plan had worked, and they could now admire the pretty rose.

John: "What are you doing out here all alone?"
Puppy: "I was running around, but then I got lost. Could you help me find my way home?"

John nodded and took the puppy in his arms. Then he got back on the horse and they rode together. Soon they had reached the puppy's house.
John: "Here we are. We made it!"

The puppy was so excited to be home again. He thanked John for his help and said goodbye. John waved goodbye, mounted his large horse, and headed back home. He was happy to have helped the puppy find his way.

Once upon a time, there lived a fat cat. His name was Tibby and he loved to play and run around. One day, Tibby found a track in the park. He decided to follow it to see what kind of adventures he could have. 

At first, the track seemed to wind around and around in circles until Tibby couldn't tell which way he was going. But then he heard a voice. It was coming from the other end of the track!

Tibby quickly ran to the end of the track and there he saw a talking mouse. The mouse said, "Hello there! Follow me and I'll show you something special." Tibby couldn't believe his eyes. He ran after the mouse and followed her around the track.

After a few more turns, Tibby and the mouse came to a small cave. Inside, Tibby found a giant bowl of ice cream! He happily licked away until the bowl was empty. When Tibby had finished, the mouse said, "Thank you for following me. I hope you had fun!"

Tibby thanked the mouse and ran home, happy and full. He never forgot his adventure on the track that day.

The next day, the orange kayak decided to spread its wings and go far away without Bob. It floated away on the water, leaving Bob behind. The orange kayak got lost and could not find its way back home. The orange kayak and Bob never saw each other again, and they both were very sad.

One day, a little girl named Mia found a sunflower seed. She went to her dependable friend, Tom. She said, "Tom, let's plant this seed and grow a big sunflower!"

Tom agreed and they planted the seed in Mia's yard. They watered it every day. Soon, a small sunflower started to grow. But one day, they saw a big bird trying to eat their sunflower.

Mia and Tom were sad. They needed to keep the bird away. Tom had an idea. He said, "Let's lock the sunflower in a cage so the bird can't eat it."

They found a cage and locked the sunflower inside. The bird could not eat it anymore. Mia and Tom were happy. Their sunflower was safe and it grew bigger and bigger. They knew they could always depend on each other to solve problems.

The boat started to go away from the port. Tim was scared. He wanted to go back to his mom, but the boat was too far from the port. Tim cried and cried, but the boat did not go back. Tim was lost, and he never saw his mom again.

The animal flew in circles and then it flew away. Everyone said goodbye to the animal and then went back to what they were doing.

But the animal never forgot about the people it had seen that day. It kept coming back to visit them, every few weeks or so. Whenever the animal showed up, everyone would stop and smile. They had found a new friend!

One day, the clouds grew dark and a storm started to brew. The wind blew hard, and it made a loud noise. The sky lit up with bright pink as lightning flashed. Everyone was scared as the storm raged on. 

What no one expected was what happened next. Suddenly, the storm revealed a beautiful rainbow! Everyone oohed and aahed in wonder. Red, orange, yellow, blue, purple and pink, the colours of the rainbow were so beautiful. 

The storm passed quickly and the rainbow stayed in the sky. It was so gorgeous, everyone cheered! After a while, the rainbow vanished, but everyone remembered its lovely pink hue.

Then, the jet started to move faster and faster, making Molly's little heart beat faster. She knew that soon, her journey would be over. 

At last, the jet glided down towards the ground. As Molly stepped out of the plane, she waved to the pilot one more time and he nodded back. She couldn't believe she had flown in a pink jet!

"Mom, please allow us to have the melon!" Anna begged. "It looks so yummy and juicy!"

"No, my dears, the melon is not ready yet. It is still green and hard. If you pick it now, it will be dead and taste bad. You have to wait until it is ripe and red," mom explained.

"But we are hungry and thirsty now!" Ben whined. "Can we have something else?"

Mom smiled and took them to the kitchen. She gave them some bread and cheese and a glass of milk. She also cut a small piece of the melon and showed it to them.

"See, this is how the melon looks inside. It is white and dry and has many seeds. It is not sweet or soft. You would not like it. But if you are patient and let it grow, it will become delicious and refreshing. Do you understand?" mom asked.

Anna and Ben nodded and tasted the melon. They made a face and spit it out. They agreed that it was not good. They thanked mom for the bread and cheese and milk and said they would wait for the melon to be ripe.

"What is that?" Sam asked, curious.

"Aw, that's no fun. It doesn't work." Lily said, disappointed.

Lily and Tom were playing with their toys in the living room. Lily had a big doll that could talk and sing. Tom had a small car that could move and beep. Lily liked her doll very much, but Tom wanted to play with it too.

"Can I have your doll for a bit?" Tom asked Lily.

"No, it's mine!" Lily said. "You have your car, play with that!"

"But your doll is more fun!" Tom said. "My car is cheap and boring!"

Tom tried to grab the doll from Lily, but Lily held it tight. They started to pull and tug, and they both complained.

"Let go of my doll!" Lily shouted.

"Give me your doll!" Tom yelled.

They pulled so hard that the doll broke in half. The head and the body fell on the floor, and the doll stopped talking and singing. Lily and Tom were shocked and sad. They both started to cry.

Their mom heard the noise and came to see what was wrong. She saw the broken doll and the crying kids, and she was angry and worried.

"What have you done?" she asked. "That doll was very expensive and special! How could you be so careless and selfish?"

She picked up the doll and tried to fix it, but it was too late. The doll was ruined. She looked at Lily and Tom, and she said:

"You are both in big trouble. You need to learn to share and be nice to each other. And you need to pay for a new doll. You will have no toys and no TV for a week. Go to your rooms now!"

Lily and Tom felt very sorry and ashamed. They wished they had not fought over the doll. They went to their rooms, still crying.

As they walked upstairs, they heard a loud siren outside. They looked out the window and saw an ambulance. It was going to their neighbor's house, where an old man lived. He had fallen down the stairs and hurt his head. He needed help.

Lily and Tom felt even more sad and scared. They wondered if the old man was okay. They wished they could help him. They wished they had not wasted their time and money on a silly doll. They realized that there were more important things in life than toys. They hugged each other and said:

"I'm sorry, I love you."

"I'm sorry, I love you too."

Lily and Sam were twins who liked to go to the park with their mom. They always took the bus to get there, because it was fun and fast. They liked to sit by the window and look at the cars, the trees, and the people.

"Shh, you can't touch that dog," she said. "That dog is working. He is helping the man who can't see."

Lily and Sam didn't understand. How could a dog help a man who can't see? They asked their mom to explain.

"The dog is called a guide dog," she said. "He is trained to follow the man's commands and lead him safely. He can sense when there is a curb, a door, or a danger. He is the man's eyes."

Lily and Sam were amazed. They thought the dog was very smart and brave. They wanted to say thank you to the dog and the man, but they didn't know how.

Their mom smiled and said, "You can say thank you with your words or your smile. But remember, don't touch the dog or distract him. He needs to focus on his job."

Lily and Sam nodded and waited for their stop. When they got off the bus, they waved and smiled at the dog and the man. The dog wagged his tail and the man said, "Thank you, kids. Have a nice day."

Lily and Sam felt happy and proud. They learned something new and made a new friend. They couldn't wait to tell their dad about the rare dog on the bus.

Tim and Mia are playing in the living room. They like to pretend they are grown-ups. Tim has a hat and a coat. Mia has a dress and a necklace. They sit on the sofa and talk.

"Hello, dear," Tim says. "How was your day?"

"Oh, very busy," Mia says. "I had to go to the shop and the park and the library."

They sip from their cups of water. They see an ashtray on the table. It is round and shiny. It has some old cigarettes in it.

"Look, Tim," Mia says. "This is what grown-ups do. They smoke and put their cigarettes in the ashtray."

"That's not good," Tim says. "Smoking is bad for you. It makes you cough and smell."

"But it looks cool," Mia says. She picks up a cigarette and puts it in her mouth. She tries to blow out some smoke.

Tim shakes his head. He picks up a lighter and tries to make a flame. He wants to strike the lighter, but he does not know how. He pushes the button hard.

Suddenly, there is a big spark and a loud noise. The lighter explodes in Tim's hand. The ashtray flies off the table and breaks on the floor. The cigarette falls out of Mia's mouth and burns a hole in the carpet.

Tim and Mia scream. They drop the lighter and the cup. They run to the door.

"Mum! Dad!" they cry. "Help! Help!"

Mum and Dad come running. They see the mess in the living room. They see the broken ashtray, the burnt carpet, the spilled water, the smoking lighter.

"What have you done?" Mum asks. "What were you thinking?"

"We're sorry, Mum," Tim says. "We were playing grown-ups."

"We wanted to be cool," Mia says.

Mum and Dad sigh. They hug Tim and Mia. They are glad they are not hurt.

"Playing grown-ups is not cool," Dad says. "It is dangerous and silly. You should never touch cigarettes or lighters. They can hurt you and make a fire."

"We understand, Dad," Tim says. "We won't do it again."

"Good," Mum says. "Now, let's tidy up this mess. And then, we'll read you a nice story."

When the race started, the animals all tried to use the missile. But they did not know how to use it. They all went very fast but in the wrong way. In the end, the slowest animal, a little turtle, won the race. The turtle cared about going the right way, not just being fast. The other animals learned that being fast is not always the best.

Once upon a time, in a small town, there was a young boy named Tim. Tim loved going to the big church with his mom and dad. The church was very pretty and had a tall tower. Tim liked to look at the tower and hear the bells ring.

One sunny day, Tim saw a little bird near the church door. The bird looked lost and sad. Tim felt the urge to help the bird. He said to the bird, "Do you need help, little bird?" The bird nodded its head.

Tim asked his mom and dad to help the bird. They all went to the church together. The little bird flew up to the tall tower and found its family. The bird was happy and sang a pretty song. Tim felt good that he helped the little bird.

One day, a big old tree and a small young tree were in the forest. The old tree was very sad because he felt dead inside. He had no more leaves and he could not grow any more. The young tree was full of life and had many green leaves.

The young tree said, "Old tree, we should unite and help each other. I can give you some of my life and you can teach me how to grow big and strong like you." The old tree thought about it and said, "Yes, let's unite and help each other."

So, the young tree shared some of its life with the old tree. The old tree started to feel better and grew some new leaves. The old tree taught the young tree how to grow tall and strong. They both became very happy.

As time went by, the young tree grew bigger and the old tree felt more alive. They were both very happy that they united and helped each other. The forest became a better place because the two trees worked together.

In the end, the old tree and the young tree lived happily together. They showed all the trees in the forest that when they unite and help each other, they can make the forest a better place for everyone.

Once upon a time, there was a cute little bird named Bobby. Bobby lived in a big tree with his family. One day, it started to rain very hard. Bobby was scared and cold, so he flew back to his tree.

When he got home, his mommy saw that he was wet and cold. She said, "Bobby, you need to stay warm and dry when it rains." She wrapped him in a soft, warm blanket. Bobby felt much better.

The next time it rained, Bobby remembered what his mommy said. He stayed in the tree with his warm blanket and watched the rain fall. He learned that it is important to listen to his mommy because she knows what is best for him. And from that day on, Bobby stayed warm and dry when it rained.

Her mom smiled and said, "Yes, we can." They made the tea and it tasted very good. Amy was happy she found the interesting herb in her garden.

Spot's owner filled the tub with warm water and put some soap in it. Spot saw the water and the soap and started to shake. His owner picked him up and gently put him in the water. Spot felt the water soak his fur and it made him feel a little better.

As Spot's owner washed him with the soap, he started to feel less frightened. The soap made bubbles that tickled his nose and made him laugh. By the end of the bath, Spot was not scared anymore. He learned that baths could be fun and not so scary after all.

Tom and Lily are brother and sister. They like to play outside with their kite. Their kite is red and blue and has a long tail. They take turns to hold the string and make the kite fly high in the sky.

One day, the wind is very strong. Tom and Lily want to fly their kite, but their mom says no. She says it is too dangerous and they might lose their kite. She tells them to behave and play with something else. Tom and Lily are sad and angry. They don't listen to their mom. They sneak out of the house with their kite.

They run to the park and find a big hill. They think they can fly their kite better there. They tie the string to a stick and put it in the ground. They let the kite go and watch it soar. They feel happy and proud. They think they are smarter than their mom.

But then, something bad happens. The wind is too strong and the string is too tight. The string snaps and the kite flies away. Tom and Lily are shocked and scared. They try to chase the kite, but it is too fast and too far. They lose their kite. They feel sad and sorry. They wish they had listened to their mom.

They go back to their house and tell their mom what happened. Their mom is not angry, but she is disappointed. She hugs them and says she loves them, but they have to learn to behave and obey. She says they can make a new kite together, but they have to be careful and respectful. Tom and Lily say they are sorry and they will behave. They hug their mom and say they love her too. They learn their lesson.

Tom and Lily went to the park with Mom. They saw a big slide, a sandbox, and some swings. Tom and Lily liked the swings best. They ran to the swings and sat on them. Mom pushed them gently.

"Look, Mom, I'm flying!" Tom said.

"Me too, me too!" Lily said.

They swung higher and higher, feeling the wind on their faces and the sun on their hair. They laughed and sang.

Suddenly, they heard a loud roar. They looked around and saw a big tiger behind the fence. The tiger had orange and black stripes, sharp teeth, and a long tail. The tiger looked hungry and angry.

"Mom, Mom, a tiger!" Tom and Lily screamed.

Mom saw the tiger too. She was scared, but she stayed calm. She grabbed Tom and Lily and ran away from the swings. She looked for a safe place to hide.

"Don't worry, kids, it's not a real tiger. It's just a toy tiger. Someone left it here as a prank. It has a speaker inside that makes the roar sound. See, it's not moving. It's just a silly joke." Mom said.

Tom and Lily looked at the toy tiger again. They saw that Mom was right. It was not a real tiger. It was just a toy tiger. They felt relieved and angry.

"That's not funny. That's mean. That scared us." Tom said.

"Yeah, that's not nice. That's rude. That made us sad." Lily said.

Mom hugged them and kissed them. She said she was sorry that someone scared them. She said they were brave and smart. She said she loved them.

"Let's go home and have some yummy cookies. How does that sound?" Mom said.

Tom and Lily smiled and nodded. They liked cookies. They were yummy. They followed Mom to the car. They forgot about the toy tiger. They were happy.

Lisa liked to play in the garage with her dad. He had many tools and machines that made loud noises and sparks. Lisa wanted to help him fix things, but he said she was too little. He gave her a plastic cup and a bottle of water to pour.

One day, Lisa saw a new machine in the garage. It was big and shiny and had many buttons and lights. Lisa thought it was very attractive. She wanted to touch it and see what it did. She asked her dad, "What is that?"

Her dad said, "That is a welder. It makes metal stick together with heat. It is very dangerous. You must not touch it or go near it. Do you understand?"

Lisa nodded, but she was still curious. She waited until her dad was busy with something else. She took her cup and bottle and walked to the welder. She poured some water on it and watched what happened.

She was not ready for the loud bang and the smoke that came out of the welder. She screamed and dropped her cup and bottle. Her dad heard her and ran to her. He saw the water and the broken welder. He was very angry and scared.

He grabbed Lisa and hugged her. He said, "Lisa, what did you do? You could have been hurt. You know you are not supposed to touch the welder. Why did you do that?"

Lisa started to cry. She said, "I'm sorry, dad. I just wanted to see it. It was so attractive. I thought water would make it happy."

Her dad sighed and said, "Lisa, water and electricity do not mix. They make fire and explosions. You must never pour water on machines. They are not like plants or animals. They do not need water to be happy. They need to be dry and safe. Do you understand?"

Lisa nodded and said, "I understand, dad. I'm sorry. I won't do it again. I love you."

Her dad said, "I love you too, Lisa. But you have to be careful and listen to me. The garage is not a place to play. It is a place to work. Come on, let's go inside and have some cookies. And then we can read a book about machines and how they work. How does that sound?"

Lisa smiled and said, "That sounds good, dad. Thank you. Can I still pour water on the plants?"

Her dad said, "Yes, you can. The plants like water. They are happy when you pour water on them. But only on the plants, okay?"

Lisa said, "Okay, dad. Only on the plants."

Lily said, "No, Tom. The knife is sharp. It can hurt you. You are too small to use the knife. Let me help you."

Tom said, "But I can do it. I am big and strong. You are silly and scared."

Lily said, "No, you are not. You are stubborn and foolish. The knife is not a toy. It is useful for grown-ups, not for kids. Give me the knife, please."

Tom did not listen to Lily. He grabbed the knife and tried to cut the potato. But the knife was too sharp and slippery. It cut his finger instead of the potato. Tom cried out loud. He dropped the knife and the potato. He ran to his mom.

Lily followed him. She felt sorry for Tom. She said, "I told you, Tom. The knife is sharp. It can hurt you. You should listen to me. I am your sister. I love you."

Tom's mom hugged him. She cleaned his wound and put a band-aid on it. She said, "Lily is right, Tom. The knife is sharp. It can hurt you. You should listen to her. She is your sister. She loves you. And I love you too. Next time, be careful and ask for help."

Tom said, "I'm sorry, mom. I'm sorry, Lily. I was wrong. The knife is sharp. It can hurt me. I should listen to you. You are my sister. You love me. And I love you too. Thank you for helping me."

Lily smiled and hugged Tom. She said, "You're welcome, Tom. I'm glad you're okay. Maybe next time, we can make potato chips together. With mom's help. They are yummy."

But the green and black ducks stayed far away. They did not want the bread. They looked at Lily and Ben with their yellow eyes. They were wild ducks. They did not accept people.

"Why don't they come, Mom?" Ben asked.

"They are not used to people. They like to be free and fly to other places. They are different from the other ducks," Mom said.

Lily and Ben nodded. They understood. They did not bother the wild ducks. They watched them swim and flap their wings. They thought the wild ducks were beautiful and brave. They learned to respect them.

Ben and Mia did not like this. They liked to take turns being the captain. And they did not want to make Rex angry. But they did not want to be rude, so they said, "OK, you can be the captain. For now. But we have to share the treasure."

Sam smiled. He said, "Deal. Come on, Rex. Let's go to the ship."

Anna and Ben were playing in the park. They liked to run and jump and slide. They saw many leaves on the ground. The leaves were red and yellow and brown. Some leaves were big and some were small. Some were thick and some were thin.

"Look, Ben, I found a thin leaf!" Anna said. She held up a leaf that was almost like paper. "It is so pretty and light. I can dress my doll with it."

Ben looked at the leaf. He thought it was too small and weak. He wanted to find a better leaf. He ran to a big tree and picked a thick leaf. "This is a good leaf," he said. "It is strong and green. I can make a hat with it."

Anna and Ben went to their dolls. They tried to dress them with their leaves. Anna wrapped the thin leaf around her doll's body. She smiled and said, "See, Ben, my doll looks like a fairy. She can fly with her leaf dress."

Ben put the thick leaf on his doll's head. He frowned and said, "No, Anna, your doll looks silly. She can't fly with that. My doll looks like a soldier. He can fight with his leaf hat."

Anna and Ben started to argue. They did not like each other's leaves. They did not want to play together. They pulled and pushed their dolls. The leaves tore and fell off. Anna and Ben cried and said, "You ruined my leaf!"

Then they heard a voice. It was their mom. She came to the park to pick them up. She saw their dolls and their leaves. She said, "Oh, Anna and Ben, what happened? Why are you crying? Why are your dolls naked?"

Anna and Ben looked at their mom. They felt ashamed and sorry. They realized they had been mean and silly. They hugged each other and said, "We're sorry, mom. We were fighting over the leaves. We wanted to dress our dolls, but we broke the leaves."

Mom smiled and said, "It's okay, my loves. I understand. You were trying to be creative and have fun. But you should also be kind and share. The leaves are beautiful, but they are not good for dressing dolls. They are too fragile and they will not last. Why don't we go home and find some real clothes for your dolls? I have some old fabric and buttons that we can use. We can make them nice and cozy."

Anna and Ben nodded and said, "Yes, mom, that sounds good. Thank you, mom. We love you, mom."

Mom took their hands and their dolls. They walked home together. They left the leaves behind. The leaves were still pretty and light. They danced in the wind. They did not mind being torn. They knew they had served their purpose. They had given Anna and Ben a lesson and a story.

Ben did not want to give it back. He liked the mirror too much. He said, "No, Lily, I want to keep it. It is mine now. I own it. You can't have it."

Lily and Ben started to argue. They both pulled on the mirror and shouted, "Mine! Mine! Mine!" They were very noisy and rude.

Tom and Lily are twins. They like to play with their cat, Max. Max is a black and white cat. He is very soft and funny. He likes to chase balls and mice.

One day, Tom and Lily find a can of tuna in the kitchen. They know that Max loves tuna. They want to give him a treat. They open the can and put some tuna in a bowl. They call Max to come and eat.

But Max does not come. He is busy playing with a ball in the living room. Tom and Lily are impatient. They want to see Max eat the tuna. They decide to take the bowl to him.

They walk to the living room with the bowl. But on the way, they meet their dog, Spot. Spot is a big and brown dog. He is very friendly and playful. He likes to run and jump.

Spot sees the bowl of tuna. He thinks it is for him. He runs to Tom and Lily and tries to take the bowl. Tom and Lily are scared. They hold the bowl tight. They do not want to give the tuna to Spot. They want to keep it for Max.

They shout at Spot. "No, Spot, no! This is not for you! This is for Max! Go away, Spot, go away!"

Spot does not understand. He thinks they are playing with him. He barks and wags his tail. He jumps and pushes. He wants the tuna.

Tom and Lily are angry. They push Spot back. They try to run to the living room. But they trip and fall. The bowl flies in the air. The tuna spills on the floor.

Tom and Lily cry. They have lost the tuna. They have made a mess. They have hurt themselves.

Sam and Lily were scared. They dropped the stick and ran away. They did not want to play with the ball anymore. They learned that some things are better left alone. And that some holes are not for poking.

Sam was curious and wanted to know more. "What plant does this root belong to?" he asked. "Can we plant it and make it grow?"

His mom shook her head and frowned. "No, Sam, we can't plant this root. This root belongs to a weed. A weed is a bad plant that grows where it is not wanted. It takes space and water from the good plants and makes them miserable."

Sam did not like the sound of that. He did not want to make the good plants miserable. He wanted to help them grow and be happy. He decided to do something about the weed root.

He took the root back from his mom and ran to the garden. He looked for the hole where he had dug it out. He saw that there were more roots and weeds around it. He grabbed a shovel and started to dig them out. He worked hard and fast until he had cleared the whole area.

He felt proud and happy. He had done a good thing for the garden. He ran back to his mom and showed her his work. "Look, Mom, I got rid of the weed root and all the other weeds. Now the good plants can grow and be happy!"

Sam smiled and hugged his mom back. He felt good and happy. He had learned something new and had fun. He loved to dig in the dirt.

Bunny was a little rabbit who loved to hop around the meadow. He liked to nibble on the grass and the carrots, but his favorite thing was to look at the sunflowers. He thought they were very pretty and bright, like the sun.

One day, he saw a very big sunflower that was taller than all the others. He wanted to see it up close, so he hopped and hopped until he reached it. He was amazed by how big and yellow it was. He wanted to touch it, so he stretched his neck and his paws.

"Hello, little rabbit," said the sunflower. "What are you doing here?"

"Hello, big sunflower," said Bunny. "You are very pretty. I wanted to touch you."

"Thank you, little rabbit. You are very kind. But be careful, you might hurt yourself. My stem is very thick and my petals are very sharp. You are too small to reach me."

Bunny felt sad. He wanted to touch the sunflower, but he could not. He wished he was bigger and stronger.

"Don't be sad, little rabbit," said the sunflower. "You are perfect the way you are. You can hop and run and play in the meadow. You have many friends and a cozy home. Bunny smiled. He realized the sunflower was right. He did not need to touch the sunflower to like it. He could be happy with what he had. He thanked the sunflower and hopped away, feeling proud of himself.

The moral of the story is: Be content with what you have and appreciate the beauty of others.

But Ben did not want to swim. He was afraid of the water. He thought it was deep and dark and had scary things. He refused to put on his life jacket. He said, "No, Lila, I don't want to swim. I want to stay on the shore and play with my truck."

Lily played with the toy car for a while, but soon she felt an itch on her arm. "Ow, ow, it hurts!" she said, scratching her arm.

"Maybe you're allergic to something," said Timmy. "Let's go ask my mom for some cream."

When they got to Timmy's house, his mom gave Lily some cream for her itch. But as she was putting it on, Lily accidentally twisted the cap too hard and the cream went everywhere! "Oops," said Lily, feeling embarrassed.

"Don't worry," said Timmy's mom. "We'll clean it up together." And they did, laughing and having fun. From that day on, Lily and Timmy became good friends and played together often.

Lily forgave her brother and they continued to play together in the bath. From that day on, Lily was more careful with her soap and her brother was more careful too.

"Okay, let's go to the mailbox first," Timmy said.

As they walked to the mailbox, Lily started to feel dizzy. She had eaten too many snacks before coming to the park. When they got to the mailbox, Lily felt so dizzy that she almost fell over.

"Are you okay, Lily?" Timmy asked, looking worried.

"I don't feel so good. I ate too many snacks," Lily said, feeling embarrassed.

"It's okay, let's sit down for a bit and then we can play catch," Timmy said, patting her back.

Lily felt better after resting for a few minutes. She mailed her letter and they played catch until it was time to go home. Even though she had eaten too many snacks, Lily was happy that she got to play with her friend.

The moral of the story is that sometimes we need to be creative and find a way to help others, even when there are obstacles in our way.

"OK!" Tom said. "But you have to promise not to cheat."

"I promise!" Lily said. "And you have to promise not to cry if I win."

"I promise!" Tom said. They shook hands and smiled.

They got ready to start the race. They counted to three and then ran as fast as they could. Lily was ahead at first, but Tom caught up with her. They reached the top of the hill at the same time. They turned around and ran down the hill. Tom stumbled and fell. Lily stopped and helped him up.

"Are you OK?" Lily asked.

"I'm OK," Tom said. "But you won the race. You are faster than me."

Lily hugged him and said, "You are very brave. And you are my best friend. The race doesn't matter."

They walked down the hill together, holding hands. They were jolly and happy. They saw their mums waiting for them. They ran to them and told them about their race. Their mums were proud of them and gave them a big hug. They had a fun day in the park.

Lily and Max were playing hide and seek in their house. Lily was the seeker and Max was the hider. Max ran upstairs to find a good spot to hide. He saw a big closet and opened the door. Inside, he found a lot of clothes and shoes and bags. He crawled behind a pile of coats and waited for Lily to come.

Lily counted to ten and then shouted, "Ready or not, here I come!" She looked around the living room and the kitchen, but she did not see Max. She thought he might be upstairs, so she went up the stairs. She checked the bedrooms and the bathroom, but she did not see Max. She wondered where he could be.

She walked to the closet and tried to open the door, but it was locked. She heard a giggle from inside. She knew it was Max. She knocked on the door and said, "Max, I found you! Come out, come out!"

Max did not want to come out. He liked his hiding place. He said, "No, you did not find me! You have to open the door first!"

Lily said, "But the door is locked. How can I open it?"

Max said, "You have to say the magic word!"

Lily thought for a moment. She remembered that their mom always told them to be obedient and polite. She said, "Please?"

Max smiled and unlocked the door. He came out of the closet and hugged Lily. He said, "You are a good seeker, Lily. And you are an obedient sister. You said the magic word!"

Lily hugged him back and said, "You are a good hider, Max. And you are a fun brother. You made me laugh!"

They went downstairs to tell their mom about their game. Their mom was proud of them for playing nicely and being obedient. She gave them a snack and a kiss. They were happy.

Lisa and Sam are playing with their toy cars and trucks. They like to make roads and bridges with blocks and cardboard. Lisa has a big truck that can load many things. Sam has a small car that is very fast.

"Look, Lisa, I can go zoom zoom with my car!" Sam says. He drives his car around the blocks and makes noises.

"That's nice, Sam, but I can load more things with my truck. See, I have a fashion doll, a teddy bear, and a book in my truck. They are going to a party!" Lisa says. She drives her truck slowly and carefully.

Sam thinks Lisa's truck is too boring. He wants to have more fun. He sees a big hill of pillows and blankets. He has an idea.

"Hey, Lisa, let's race to the top of the hill! The first one to get there wins!" Sam says.

"OK, Sam, but be careful. Don't crash into my truck or the things in it. They are very important to me." Lisa says.

Sam nods, but he is too excited to listen. He drives his car very fast and careless. He bumps into Lisa's truck and makes it tip over. The fashion doll, the teddy bear, and the book fall out and get dirty.

"Sam, what did you do? You ruined my things! You are very bad!" Lisa cries. She picks up her things and hugs them.

"I'm sorry, Lisa, I didn't mean to. I just wanted to have fun. Please don't be mad at me." Sam says. He feels sorry and sad.

Lisa looks at Sam and sees his sad face. She remembers that he is her friend and that he didn't do it on purpose. She decides to forgive him.

"It's OK, Sam, I'm not mad at you. But you have to be more careful next time. And you have to help me clean my things. OK?" Lisa says.

"OK, Lisa, I will. And I will share my car with you. Do you want to play with it?" Sam says.

"Yes, Sam, I do. And I will share my truck with you. Do you want to load some things in it?" Lisa says.

"Yes, Lisa, I do. Let's play together." Sam says.

They smile and hug. They play with their cars and trucks and have fun. They are good friends. The end.

Ben and Lily were friends who liked to play together. They went to the same school and had the same teacher. One day, their teacher said they could go to the gym and have fun. Ben and Lily were very happy and ran to the gym.

The gym had many toys and games. There were balls, hoops, mats, slides, and swings. Ben and Lily wanted to try everything. But Ben was selfish. He did not want to share with Lily or anyone else. He took the biggest ball and the highest swing and said, "These are mine. You can't have them."

Lily was sad and angry. She said, "That's not fair, Ben. You are selfish. You have to share with your friends. We can take turns and play together." But Ben did not listen. He said, "No, I don't. I like these toys and I want them all. Go away, Lily. Find something else."

Lily felt hurt and lonely. She looked around and saw a nice girl with a hoop. The girl smiled and said, "Hi, I'm Mia. Do you want to play with me? We can share my hoop and make circles." Lily smiled back and said, "Yes, please. I'm Lily. Thank you for sharing, Mia. You are kind."

Mia and Lily became friends and had fun with the hoop. They made circles and laughed. Ben saw them and felt jealous. He wanted to join them, but he was too proud to say sorry. He stayed on his swing and played alone. He realized that being selfish was not fun at all.

Mia raises her hand. She knows the answer. She says, "That is a square, Miss Lee. A square has four sides and four corners."

Ben and Mia smile. They are happy. They like Miss Lee. They like to learn new things. They are good friends.

"Let's look in the hole," Anna says. She bends down and puts her head in the hole. She sees something furry and brown. It looks like a big ball.

"Stop, it hurts!" Anna says. She cries. She runs to their mom, who is sitting on a bench nearby.

"Mom, mom, help!" Anna says. She shows her mom the squirrel tail.

"It's okay, sweetie, it's just a squirrel. He was probably scared and grabbed your hair. He didn't mean to hurt you," Mom says.

"Sorry, Anna, I didn't mean to laugh," Ben says. He hugs Anna too. He says sorry to the squirrel.

"Let's go home and have some cookies," Mom says. She takes Anna and Ben by the hand. They leave the forest and walk to their house. They are happy again.

Tom and Lily liked to go to the park and feed the swans. They brought bread and threw it in the water. The swans came and ate the bread. They were white and big and had long necks. Tom and Lily thought they were beautiful.

One day, they saw a swan that had a broken wing. It could not fly or swim well. It looked sad and hurt. Tom and Lily felt sorry for it. They wanted to help it.

"Can we repair the swan's wing?" Lily asked Tom.

"I don't know. Maybe we can find someone who knows how to fix it," Tom said.

They looked around and saw a man with a green hat and a bag. He had a badge that said "Park Ranger". He looked friendly and kind.

"Excuse me, sir. Can you help us?" Tom said.

The man looked at them and smiled. He saw the swan with the broken wing.

"Hello, children. What can I do for you?" he said.

"We want to help this swan. It has a broken wing. Can you repair it?" Lily said.

The man nodded. He took out some bandages and a scissors from his bag. He gently picked up the swan and wrapped its wing with the bandages. He cut off the extra part with the scissors.

"There. This should help the swan heal. It will take some time, but it will be able to fly and swim again soon," he said.

He put the swan back in the water. The swan looked happier and thanked the man with a honk.

"Thank you, sir. You are very nice," Tom said.

"You're welcome, children. You are very brave and caring. You did the right thing by asking for help. Some people are ignorant and don't care about the swans. They throw trash or stones at them. That's very bad and mean. You should always respect and protect the animals," the man said.

Tom and Lily nodded. They agreed with the man. They loved the swans and wanted them to be happy and healthy.

They waved goodbye to the man and the swan. They decided to come back to the park and visit the swan again. They hoped it would get better soon. They were proud of themselves for helping the swan. They learned a new word: repair. They also learned a new lesson: don't be ignorant.

Lily and Tom were twins who liked to play in the garden. One day, they saw a shiny thing under a big rock. They moved the rock and found a small box. Inside the box, there were many coins that looked like gold.

"Wow, look at this!" Lily said. "We are rich!"

"Let's take them home and buy lots of toys and candy!" Tom said.

They put the box in their wagon and started to pull it. But the box was very heavy and the wagon was very slow. They got tired and thirsty.

"Can we stop and drink some water?" Lily asked.

"No, we have to hurry. Someone might see our gold and take it!" Tom said.

They kept walking until they reached a fountain. There, they saw a man who was smiling and playing a flute. He had a hat with many flowers and a coat with many colors. He looked very charming.

"Hello, children. What do you have in your wagon?" the man asked.

"It's none of your business!" Tom said. He did not trust the man.

"It's our gold. We found it in the garden and we are going to buy everything we want!" Lily said. She wanted to show off.

"Gold, you say? That's very interesting. Can I see it?" the man asked.

He reached for the box, but Tom pulled it away.

"No, you can't! It's ours!" Tom said.

The man laughed. "Don't be so greedy, my friends. Do you know what gold is? Do you know what it tastes like?"

"Tastes like? Gold is not for eating, silly!" Lily said.

"Are you sure? Why don't you try it? Maybe it's delicious. Maybe it's better than water or candy. Go on, take a bite!" the man said.

He took a coin from the box and handed it to Lily. She was curious and hungry, so she put it in her mouth. But it was hard and bitter and hurt her teeth. She spat it out and made a face.

"Yuck! This is not gold! This is metal!" she said.

The man laughed again. "That's right, my dear. This is not gold. This is brass. It's worthless. Someone must have buried it as a joke. You have been fooled!"

Lily and Tom felt ashamed and angry. They had wasted their time and energy for nothing. They had been rude and selfish. They had ignored their thirst and their friendliness.

They looked at the man, who was still smiling and playing his flute. He had no gold, but he had music and joy. He had water and flowers. He had charm and kindness.

They realized that he was richer than they were. They realized that they had been wrong.

They thanked the man and gave him the box of brass. They did not want it anymore. They took their wagon and went home. They decided to share their toys and their candy with their friends. They decided to be more careful and more generous.

They learned that gold is not everything. They learned that taste is not only in the mouth, but also in the heart. They learned that charming is not only in the eyes, but also in the soul.

But Max did not listen to Lily. He was stubborn and kept trying to open the bottle. He did not care about the mess. He just wanted some juice.

Then, suddenly, the bottle popped open. The juice poured out and spilled everywhere. It splashed on the floor, on the couch, on the table, and on Lily and Max. They were wet and sticky and covered in juice. They looked at each other and gasped.

"Oh no!" Lily said. "Look what you did, Max! You made a big mess! Mommy will be so mad! She will take us to the hospital and give us a shot!"

Ben and Lily shook their heads. They wanted to know more. Mom and dad explained, "A rainbow is a special thing that happens when the sun shines on the rain. The raindrops act like tiny mirrors and split the sunlight into different colors. That's why you see a rainbow in the sky."

Ben and Lily nodded. They understood a little bit. They said, "Thank you, mom and dad. We like rainbows. They make us happy."

Mom and dad hugged them and said, "We're happy too. You are our little rainbows. You make our garden more colorful and wonderful."

They are scared. They know they did something bad.

The goat heard Tom and looked up. It saw Tom and Spot running towards it. It did not like them. It thought they were scary. It bleated, "Baa!" and ran away. Tom and Spot chased the goat. They made a lot of noise.

Tom and Lily were sorry and scared. They dropped the bowl and ran to their room. They did not eat any oats. They did not have any fun. They had a bad day.

But then, Ben saw a big puddle near the fence. He ran to it and jumped in. He made a big splash and got very wet. He was happy.

Anna was angry. She said, "That is not fair. You have to share. I want to jump in the puddle too!"

Anna and Ben started to complain. They shouted and pushed each other. They did not have fun anymore.

Anna and Ben nodded. They said, "Sorry, Ben. Sorry, Anna. We are friends again."

One day, a little girl named Lily wanted to go outside and play with her ball. But her mom said, "No, Lily, you cannot go outside. There is a big storm coming. It is very dark and loud and wet. You have to stay inside and be safe."

Lily did not listen to her mom. She was very stubborn. She said, "I want to go outside. I want to play with my ball. I do not care about the storm. You are mean, mom." She complain and complain and complain.

Her mom said, "Lily, stop complaining. You have to obey me. I know what is best for you. The storm is dangerous. You can play with your ball later. Why don't you play with your toys or read a book or draw a picture?"

Lily did not want to do any of those things. She only wanted to go outside and play with her ball. She sneak out of the house when her mom was not looking. She ran to the yard and kicked her ball. She was happy for a little while.

But then, the storm came. It was very dark and loud and wet. The wind blew hard and the rain fell fast. Lily was scared. She could not see her ball. She could not see her house. She could not hear her mom. She was cold and wet and alone. She cried and cried and cried.

Her mom heard her cry. She ran outside and found her. She hugged her and said, "Lily, I am so glad you are okay. I was so worried about you. You should not have gone outside. You should have listened to me. The storm is dangerous. You could have been hurt."

Lily said, "I am sorry, mom. I was very stubborn. I complain and complain and complain. I did not obey you. I did not know what is best for me. You were right, mom. The storm is dangerous. I should have stayed inside and be safe."

Her mom said, "It's okay, Lily. I forgive you. I love you. But you have to learn from your mistake. Next time, you have to listen to me and do what I say. I only want you to be happy and safe. Do you understand?"

Lily said, "Yes, mom. I understand. I love you too. Can we go inside now?"

Her mom said, "Yes, Lily. Let's go inside and dry off. You can play with your ball later when the storm is over."

Lily said, "Okay, mom. Thank you, mom."

They went inside and cuddled on the couch. They watched the storm pass by. They were happy and safe.

The moral of the story is: You should listen to your parents and obey them. They know what is best for you. They only want you to be happy and safe. You should not be stubborn and complain. You should be grateful and respectful.

"Hello, Lily. I'm Dr. Lee. I'm going to look at you and see what's wrong. Don't worry, it won't hurt," he said.

Lily did not believe him. She was afraid. She clung to her mom and cried. She did not want the doctor to touch her. She did not want to be sick.

The doctor tried to calm her down. He said he was her friend. He said he wanted to help her. He said he had a surprise for her. He reached for his pocket and took out something.

Lily stopped crying. She looked at the doctor's hand. She saw a shiny metal thing. It was a needle. The doctor was lying. He wanted to hurt her. He wanted to poke her with the needle.

Lily screamed. She kicked and bit the doctor. She ran out of the room. She ran back to the big room. She ran to Ben. She wanted to be with him. He was her friend. He understood her.

Lily was alone. She was scared. She was sick. She wished she had listened to the doctor. She wished she had been patient and brave. She wished she had not run away. She wished she had not lost her friend.

The man saw Lily. He pointed the gun at her. He pulled the trigger. Lily closed her eyes. She did not feel anything. She did not hear anything. She did not see anything.

The end.

He thought it was a good time to play his trumpet. He went to his room and took out his trumpet. He blew it as hard as he could. He made a wild noise.

His sister was trying to sleep. She heard the wild noise and got angry. She went to Tom's room and knocked on the door. She told him to stop playing his trumpet. But Tom did not listen. He kept playing his trumpet. He locked the door and did not let his sister in. He thought he was smart and funny.

But he was not smart and funny. He was mean and rude. He did not know that his mom and dad had a spare key. They came back early and heard the wild noise. They went to Tom's room and unlocked the door. They saw Tom playing his trumpet. They were not happy. They took away his trumpet and scolded him. They told him he was selfish and naughty. They told him he had to share and be kind.

Tom felt sorry. He realized he was wrong. He apologized to his mom, dad, and sister. He promised to play his trumpet only when it was okay. He learned his lesson. He learned that playing his trumpet was fun, but not when it hurt others. He learned that being wild was not good, but being nice was.

Tim and Lily were twins who liked to eat waffles for breakfast. One morning, their mom made them waffles with syrup and butter. She put the waffles on two plates and told them to eat nicely.

Tim and Lily took their plates and sat at the table. They looked at their waffles and smiled. They were hungry and happy. But then, Tim had a question.

"Mom, can I have more syrup?" he asked.

"Sure, honey, but don't put too much. You don't want your waffle to be too wet and sticky," mom said.

She gave him the bottle of syrup and went to the kitchen. Tim poured some syrup on his waffle, but he wanted more. He poured and poured until his waffle was covered with syrup. It looked like a brown lake.

Lily saw what Tim did and shook her head. She thought he was silly. She only put a little syrup on her waffle. She liked it that way. She took a bite and said, "Mmm, this is good."

Tim took a bite of his waffle too, but he did not say anything. He felt the syrup in his mouth and on his fingers. It was too sweet and sticky. He did not like it. He made a face and said, "Blech, this is bad."

He tried to eat more, but he could not. He felt sick. He pushed his plate away and said, "I don't want this."

Mom came back and saw Tim's plate. She was surprised and sad. She said, "Tim, what did you do? You wasted your waffle and the syrup. You should have listened to me. Too much of anything is not good for you."

Tim felt sorry and ashamed. He said, "I'm sorry, mom. I was greedy. I should have listened to you. Can I have another waffle, please?"

Mom said, "No, Tim. You had your chance. You have to learn from your mistake. Maybe next time you will be more careful and thankful. Now, go wash your hands and face. They are wet and sticky."

Tim nodded and went to the bathroom. He wished he had eaten his waffle like Lily. He learned a lesson that day. He learned that more is not always better, and that he should listen to his mom. He hoped that tomorrow he would have another chance to eat a waffle nicely.

When Sam comes back to the garden, he sees the jar. He sees the bird. He sees the mess. He feels sad and angry. He cries and shouts at the bird. He thinks the bird is mean and rude. He wishes he could save the worms. He misses his worm friends.

Lily and Max went to the museum with Mom and Dad. They saw many things that were old and new. They saw big bones of animals that were not alive anymore. They saw shiny rocks that had many colors. They saw paintings and statues that people made a long time ago.

"What is he doing?" Lily asked.

"Wow, that is amazing!" Max said.

"Look, kids, this is a tooth of a tyrannosaurus rex!" he said. "It was very big and sharp. It could bite through anything."

"Wow, that is awesome!" Lily and Max said.

They were very happy and excited. They thanked the man who worked at the museum and the man who dug for fossils. They learned a lot and had a lot of fun. They loved the museum and wanted to come back again.

"Yes, please, Sara. You are very kind," Mr. Bear said in a low voice.

"And how about you, Miss Doll? Do you want some tea?" Ben asked, doing the same.

"Of course, Ben. You are very nice," Miss Doll said in a high voice.

Sara and Ben smiled and sipped their tea. They felt very happy and proud of their tea party. They did not know that a naughty cat was watching them from behind a bush. The cat was hungry and wanted to eat their teddy bears and dolls. He waited for the right moment to pounce.

Suddenly, the cat jumped out of the bush and ran towards the tea party. He knocked over the cups and plates and grabbed Mr. Bear in his mouth. He also tried to snatch Miss Doll, but Ben held her tight.

"Help! Help! The cat is taking Mr. Bear!" Sara cried.

"Ow! Ow! Stop that!" the cat yowled.
