"Good job, Sara!" Ben praised, lowering her down.

Lily and Ben were twins who lived in a big house near a valley. They liked to play with their toys and their dog, Spot. One day, their mom said they could go to the store with her. They were very happy and put on their coats and shoes.

At the store, they saw many things they wanted. Lily saw a doll with a pink dress and long hair. Ben saw a truck with big wheels and a horn. They both asked their mom if they could have them. Their mom said they could only choose one thing each. Lily and Ben could not agree on what to choose. They started to argue and cry.

Their mom was not happy. She said they had to stop fighting or they would go home without anything. Lily and Ben did not want that. They looked at each other and felt sorry. They decided to share their toys and play together. They told their mom they were sorry and hugged her.

Their mom smiled and said they were good children. She bought them the doll and the truck and gave them a kiss. They thanked her and said they loved her. They went back to their big house near the valley. They played with their toys and their dog, Spot. They had a lot of fun and were very happy. They thought their mom was the best and their toys were adorable.

Lily and Max were very happy to go to the circus. They wanted to see the clowns and the animals and the tricks. They got in the car with Mom and Dad and drove to the big tent.

When they got there, they saw a lot of people and a lot of noise. They followed Mom and Dad to their seats and waited for the show to start. They saw a man with a big hat and a big smile. He was the ringmaster. He said, "Welcome to the circus! We have a lot of fun for you today!"

The first act was the clowns. They came out of a small car and made everyone laugh. They had big shoes and big noses and funny clothes. They did silly things and threw pies and squirted water. Lily and Max liked the clowns a lot.

But then, something bad happened. One of the clowns had a suitcase. He wanted to unpack it and show everyone what was inside. But when he opened it, nothing came out. He looked inside and saw that everything was broken. His toys, his clothes, his hat, his wig, everything was broken. He was very sad. He started to cry.

The other clowns tried to cheer him up. They gave him hugs and jokes and balloons. But he did not stop crying. He said, "Someone broke my things! Who did it? Who was mean to me?"

Lily and Max felt sorry for the clown. They wanted to help him. They looked around and saw a boy with a mean face. He had a stick in his hand. He was the one who broke the clown's things. He was hiding behind a seat. He was laughing.

Lily and Max got up and walked to the boy. They said, "You are bad! You broke the clown's things! You made him sad! You should say sorry!"

The boy was surprised. He did not think anyone saw him. He was scared. He said, "No, I did not! It was not me! Go away!"

But Lily and Max did not go away. They said, "Yes, you did! We saw you! You are lying! You should be nice!"

The boy did not know what to do. He dropped his stick and ran away. He did not want to get in trouble.

Lily and Max picked up the stick and went to the clown. They said, "We are sorry for what he did. He was bad. He ran away. Here is his stick. Maybe you can use it for something."

The clown looked at them and smiled. He wiped his tears and said, "Thank you, Lily and Max. You are very kind. You are very brave. You are my friends. Here, take this." He gave them each a balloon. He said, "This is for you. You made me happy. You are the best."

Lily and Max smiled back. They said, "You are welcome, clown. You are funny. You are our friend. You are the best."

They hugged the clown and went back to their seats. They watched the rest of the show and had a lot of fun. They learned that it is good to be nice and bad to be mean. They learned that clowns are people too. They learned that they can make a difference. They were very happy.

Tom and Anna liked to jog with their dad every morning. They put on their shoes and hats and went outside. They saw the sun and the birds and the flowers. They jogged on the path and said hello to the people and the dogs they met.

One day, they jogged to the bakery. They smelled something good. It was bread and cake and cookies. They went inside and saw a huge oven. The baker was taking out a tray of muffins. He smiled and said, "Do you want to try one? They are hot and yummy."

Tom and Anna nodded and said, "Yes, please!" The baker gave them each a muffin and a glass of milk. They thanked him and sat on a table. They bit into the muffins and felt the warm and sweet taste. They liked them very much. They said, "These are the best muffins ever!"

The baker laughed and said, "I'm glad you like them. You can have another one if you want. You must be hungry after jogging so much." Tom and Anna smiled and said, "Yes, we are. Thank you, baker. You are very nice."

They finished their muffins and milk and said goodbye to the baker. They jogged back home with their dad. They told their mom about the bakery and the huge oven and the muffins. They said, "We had a fun and tasty morning!"

Lily and Max were playing in the yard. They saw a big pile of junk near the fence. It had old cans, boxes, wires and other things. Lily wanted to go and look at the junk. She thought it might have something fun or shiny inside.

"Come on, Max, let's go and see the junk!" she said.

Max shook his head. He did not want to go near the junk. He thought it might be dirty or sharp or hurt them.

"No, Lily, we can't go there. It's not safe. Mom said to stay away from the junk. It's bad for us," he said.

Lily did not listen to Max. She wanted to see the junk. She ran towards the pile. Max tried to stop her. He grabbed her hand and pulled her back.

"Lily, stop! Don't go there! Please!" he said.

Lily tried to resist. She pulled her hand away from Max. She was angry at him. She thought he was being silly and scared.

"Let me go, Max! You're no fun! I want to see the junk! It's not bad, it's cool!" she said.

She ran to the junk and started to dig in it. She found a shiny can and a colorful box. She smiled and picked them up. She did not see the wire that was sticking out of the junk. It was sharp and had electricity in it. It touched her leg and gave her a big shock. She screamed and dropped the can and the box. She fell to the ground and cried.

Max heard her scream and ran to her. He saw the wire and the junk. He was scared and sad. He hugged her and called for help.

"Lily, Lily, are you okay? I'm sorry, I'm sorry. I was trying to keep you safe. Mom, dad, help!" he said.

Mom and dad heard Max and Lily and came to the yard. They saw the junk and the wire and Lily. They were shocked and worried. They took Lily to the house and called the doctor. They checked her leg and gave her a bandage and a hug. They told her she was brave and lucky. They told her to never go near the junk again. They told her to listen to Max and to mom and dad. They told her they loved her.

Lily felt sorry and ashamed. She realized she was wrong and Max was right. She apologized to Max and to mom and dad. She thanked them for helping her and caring for her. She told them she loved them too.

She learned a lesson that day. She learned to stay away from the junk. She learned to be safe. She learned to listen. She learned to resist her curiosity when it was dangerous. She learned to appreciate her brother and her parents. She learned to be more careful and more fun.

Lily was sad. She missed her mom and dad. They went to work and left her with Nana. Nana was nice, but Lily wanted her mom and dad.

Nana saw Lily crying on the couch. She came over and hugged her. "What's wrong, Lily?" she asked.

"I want mom and dad," Lily sobbed.

Nana comforted Lily. She said, "Mom and dad love you very much. They will come back soon. Do you want to do something fun with me?"

Lily nodded. She liked fun things.

Nana smiled. She said, "Let's make some music. You are very creative. You can sing and play with these instruments." She showed Lily a box of toys that made sounds. There was a drum, a bell, a whistle, and a xylophone.

Lily wiped her tears. She felt a little better. She said, "OK, Nana. Let's make music."

Nana and Lily made music together. They sang songs and played with the instruments. They made loud noises and soft noises. They made happy noises and silly noises. They laughed and clapped.

Lily forgot about being sad. She had fun with Nana. She felt loved and happy. She said, "Thank you, Nana. You are the best."

Nana hugged Lily. She said, "You are welcome, Lily. You are the best, too."

"Look, Anna, red fruits!" Tom says. "Let's pick some."

"OK, Tom, but be careful. The tree is very high." Anna says.

Tom and Anna run to the tree. They gaze at the red fruits. They look yummy. Tom climbs on a branch. He reaches for a fruit. He picks it and bites it. It is sweet and juicy.

"Yum, yum, this is good!" Tom says. "Here, Anna, catch!"

He throws a fruit to Anna. She catches it and bites it. She likes it too.

"Yum, yum, this is good!" Anna says. "Thank you, Tom!"

They smile and eat more fruits. They are happy.

But then, they hear a loud roar. They look down. They see a big bear. The bear is angry. It wants the fruits too. It shakes the tree. Tom and Anna are fearful. They hold on to the branch. They scream.

"Help, help, a bear!" Tom says.

"Help, help, a bear!" Anna says.

They hope someone will hear them and save them. They are very scared.

Tom was sad. He missed his dad. His dad was far away. He worked in a big ship. He sent Tom mail every week. Tom liked to read his dad's mail. It had pictures and stickers and jokes.

One day, Tom did not get any mail. He waited and waited. He asked his mom, "Where is dad's mail?"

Mom said, "I don't know, Tom. Maybe the mail is late. Maybe the ship is in a place where there is no mail. Don't worry, Tom. Dad loves you. He will send you mail soon."

Tom felt sad. He wanted to hear from his dad. He wanted to see his dad. He hugged his mom. Mom hugged him back. She said, "I love you, Tom. I am here to comfort you. We can do something fun. Do you want to play a game? Do you want to read a book? Do you want to bake a cake?"

Tom nodded. He said, "Yes, mom. I want to do all those things. But can we also check the mail later?"

Mom smiled. She said, "Of course, Tom. We can check the mail later. Maybe there will be a surprise for you."

Tom smiled too. He said, "Maybe, mom. Maybe there will be a thick mail from dad. A mail with lots of pictures and stickers and jokes. A mail that says he is coming home soon."

Mom said, "That would be wonderful, Tom. That would be the best mail ever."

Tom and Mia were playing in the yard. They had a big box of gear. Gear was things that you could use to make other things. They liked to make cars and planes and robots with gear.

But Tom wanted to make a big rocket. He said, "I need more gear. I will cut this box and use it for my rocket." He took a pair of scissors and started to cut the box.

Mia was troubled. She said, "No, Tom, don't cut the box. That is our gear box. We need it to keep our gear. If you cut it, we will lose our gear."

Tom did not listen. He said, "I don't care. I want a big rocket. Go away, Mia." He cut the box more and more.

Mia was very sad. She ran to the house and told Mom. Mom came to the yard and saw what Tom had done. She was angry. She said, "Tom, you are very naughty. You cut the gear box and made a mess. You hurt Mia's feelings. You have to say sorry to Mia and help her clean up the yard."

Tom felt bad. He saw that he had been selfish and mean. He said, "I'm sorry, Mia. I'm sorry, Mom. I was wrong to cut the gear box. I don't need a big rocket. I need you and our gear. Can we play together again?"

Mia smiled. She said, "It's okay, Tom. I forgive you. Let's play together again. We can make something else with our gear. Maybe a boat or a train or a castle."

Mom hugged them both. She said, "I'm glad you are friends again. You can play with your gear, but be careful with the scissors. And don't cut anything without asking me first."

Tom and Mia nodded. They put their gear back in the box and taped it together. They played happily with their gear and each other. They learned to share and be kind.

"Let's go inside and pretend we live here," Lily said.

"What is that?" Lily asked.

"It's spicy sauce. It makes food taste good. I want to put some on the snow and eat it," Sam said.

"Yuck! That sounds gross. Don't do that. You will spoil the snow and our igloo," Lily said.

"No, I won't. It will be yummy. Watch me," Sam said. He poured some sauce on a handful of snow and put it in his mouth.

"Aaaah! Hot! Hot! Hot!" Sam screamed. He spit out the snow and ran to his house. His tongue was burning.

Lily shook her head. She went inside the igloo and closed the door. She was glad she did not try the spicy sauce. She liked the snow just the way it was. She hoped Sam would be OK. She also hoped he would not spoil their igloo again.

Tom and Lily were playing in the living room. They had many toys, but they liked the carpet best. The carpet was soft and colorful, and they could pretend it was a magic carpet that flew them to different places.

"Let's go to the zoo!" Lily said. She put her stuffed animals on the carpet and made animal noises.

But then, Tom saw a big hole in the carpet. He was curious and put his finger in the hole. He felt something hard and sharp. He pulled out a nail.

"Look, Lily, I found a nail!" Tom said. He showed the nail to Lily.

"Where did you get that?" Lily asked. She looked at the carpet and saw the hole. She gasped. "Oh no, the carpet is broken! Mom will be mad!"

Tom and Lily were scared. They did not want Mom to be mad. They tried to hide the hole with their toys, but it was too big. They heard Mom coming down the stairs.

"Tom, Lily, what are you doing?" Mom asked. She saw the toys on the carpet and smiled. She thought they were having fun.

But then, she saw the nail in Tom's hand and the hole in the carpet. She frowned. She was not happy.

"Tom, Lily, did you do this?" Mom asked. She pointed at the hole and the nail.

Lila was a gifted girl who could draw very well. She liked to make pictures of animals, flowers and people. She had many crayons and papers in her room. She was happy when she could share her drawings with her friends and family.

One day, she wanted to draw a picture of her mom. She looked at her mom's dress and saw that it was blue and white. She thought it was very pretty. She wanted to wear it too. She asked her mom, "Can I wear your dress, please?"

Her mom smiled and said, "No, Lila. This dress is too big for you. And it is not for playing. It is for going out. You have your own dresses that fit you and are for playing. Why don't you wear one of them?"

Lila was sad. She did not want to wear her own dresses. She wanted to wear her mom's dress. She thought it would make her draw better. She waited until her mom was busy in the kitchen. Then she sneaked into her mom's room and took her dress. She put it on over her clothes. It was very big and long. She tripped over it as she walked. She did not care. She felt like a grown-up.

She went to her room and took her crayons and papers. She started to draw a picture of her mom. She wanted to make it very nice. She used many colors and shapes. She was so focused on her drawing that she did not notice that her crayons were making marks on her mom's dress. She also did not notice that her brother had left a jar of butter on the floor. She stepped on it and slipped. The butter spilled all over her mom's dress. She fell down and hurt her knee. She cried.

Her mom heard her cry and came to her room. She saw Lila on the floor, wearing her dress, covered in butter and crayon marks. She was shocked and angry. She said, "Lila, what have you done? You ruined my dress! You disobeyed me! You were very naughty!"

Lila felt sorry and ashamed. She said, "I'm sorry, mom. I wanted to wear your dress and draw a picture of you. I thought it would make me more gifted. But I made a mess and hurt myself. I was very silly."

Her mom hugged her and said, "Lila, you don't need to wear my dress to be gifted. You are gifted because you have a talent and a passion for drawing. You can draw beautiful pictures with your own clothes and your own crayons. But you also need to respect other people's things and listen to their words. That is what makes you a good person. Do you understand?"

Lila nodded and said, "Yes, mom. I understand. I'm sorry for ruining your dress. I love you."

Her mom said, "I love you too, Lila. Now let's clean up this mess and put some ice on your knee. And then you can show me your picture of me. I'm sure it is very nice."

The end.

Tom and Lily were playing in the park. They liked to run and jump and slide. They saw a big zip that went from one tree to another. They wanted to try it.

"Let's go on the zip!" Tom said.

"OK!" Lily said.

They ran to the zip and took turns to hold the handle and slide to the other tree. It was fun and fast. They laughed and shouted.

But then, something bad happened. Tom saw some smoke and fire near the zip. Someone had left a fire there and it was burning the rope. Tom was scared.

"Lily, look! The zip is burning!" Tom said.

Lily looked and saw the fire too. She was scared too.

"Oh no! What do we do?" Lily said.

They did not know how to stop the fire. They did not see anyone who could help them. They thought the zip would break and fall. They felt terrible.

They decided to run away from the fire and the zip. They ran to the other side of the park and looked for their mom and dad. They found them and told them what happened.

"Mom, Dad, the zip is burning!" Tom said.

"The zip is burning?" Mom said.

"Yes, there is a fire and it is burning the rope!" Lily said.

Mom and Dad were shocked. They took Tom and Lily and went to see the fire. They saw the zip was still burning and no one was there. They called the firemen to come and put out the fire.

The firemen came and used water and foam to stop the fire. They saved the zip and the trees. They told Tom and Lily that they were brave and smart to run away from the fire and tell their parents.

Tom and Lily were happy that the fire was gone and the zip was safe. They thanked the firemen and hugged their mom and dad. They learned that fire can be dangerous and they should never play with it. They also learned that the zip was fun and they wanted to try it again. But only when there was no fire.

But then, a big wind comes. It blows very hard. It makes Tim and his mom and the snowman very cold. Tim feels his nose and fingers and toes freeze. He does not like it. He says, "Mom, I want to go inside!"

His mom says, "OK, Tim, let's go inside. It is too bitter outside. We can do some math inside. That will warm us up."

Tim and his mom go inside. They take off their coat and hat and boots and gloves. They sit on the couch with a blanket and a cup of hot chocolate. They do some math with Tim's book. They count and add and take away. They are happy. They say, "We like math!"

One night, Tom and Lily wanted to see an owl. They put on their warm coats and hats and went outside with their dad. They walked to the big tree where dad said the owl lived.

"Shh, be quiet," dad whispered. "We don't want to scare the owl away."

They looked up at the tree and saw a big shadow. It was the owl! It had big eyes and a round head and a rough feather coat. It looked at them and said, "Hoo, hoo, hoo."

"Wow, it's so cool!" Tom said.

"Can we touch it?" Lily asked.

"No, we can't," dad said. "The owl is wild and might bite or scratch. We can only watch and listen."

They watched and listened for a while, until the owl flew away. They saw its big wings and heard its soft sound.

"Bye, owl!" Tom and Lily said.

"Let's hurry back home," dad said. "It's late and cold and we need to sleep."

They hurried back home and got into their beds. They dreamed of the owl and the big tree and the night sky. They were happy.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Sue. Sue loved to play in her backyard. One day, she found a shiny crystal on the ground. The crystal was very pretty, but it was also dangerous. Sue knew she should not touch it.

Sue ran to her mom and said, "Mom, I found a crystal. It is pretty, but I think it is dangerous. What should I do?" Her mom thought for a moment and said, "Sue, you are a smart girl. Let's accept that the crystal is dangerous and put it in a safe place."

So, Sue and her mom found a box to put the crystal in. They put the box on a high shelf where no one could reach it. Sue felt happy that she had done the right thing.

From that day on, Sue always remembered to be careful with things she found. She knew that some things could be pretty but also dangerous. Sue and her mom were very proud of their smart decision. And they lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time, in a small village, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim loved to play outside with his friends all day long. One day, while playing near the woods, Tim heard a distant voice. He stopped and tried to listen.

Tim and the bird became good friends. They played together every day. Tim learned to listen to the voices of others, even if they were distant. And the bird learned that there are good people in the world who will help when you need it.

The moral of the story is to always listen and be kind to others, no matter how small or distant they may seem.

One day, the train saw a big hill. The train wanted to go up the hill, but it was scared. It did not know if it could do it. The train thought and thought. Then, it said, "I dare to go up the hill!"

The train started to go up the hill. It went slow at first, but then it went faster and faster. The train made lots of steam as it went up the hill. The people in the town watched and cheered for the train.

When the train got to the top of the hill, it was very happy. It had dared to go up the hill and made it. The train went down the hill and back to the town. The people clapped and smiled. The beautiful train was proud and knew it could do anything it dared to do.

Tim and Kim are twins. They like to play in the park. One day, they find a shiny coin on the ground. It is gold and round.

"Wow, look at this!" Tim says. "It is so pretty!"

"Let me see!" Kim says. She tries to grab the coin from Tim.

"No, it is mine!" Tim says. He holds the coin tight.

They start to fight over the coin. They pull and push and shout.

A man sees them and comes over. He is wearing a hat and a coat. He looks at the coin and smiles.

"Hello, kids," he says. "Do you know what this is?"

"It is a gold coin!" Tim says.

"It is ours!" Kim says.

The man shakes his head. "No, it is not. It is a chocolate coin. It is a candy. You can eat it."

He peels off the gold paper and breaks the coin in half. He gives one half to Tim and one half to Kim.

"Here, taste it," he says. "It is sweet and yummy."

Tim and Kim take a bite. They make a face. The chocolate is old and dry. It does not taste good.

"Yuck!" Tim says.

"Bleh!" Kim says.

They spit out the chocolate and throw away the paper.

"Thank you, mister," they say. "But we do not like this coin."

They run away and look for something else to play with. The man laughs and walks away. He thinks they are funny.

Anna and Ben sighed. They followed mom to a store that had many shirts. Mom looked at the shirts and picked some for them to try on. Anna and Ben did not like the shirts. They were terrible. They were scratchy and ugly and had no planes on them.

"Mom, we don't like these shirts," Ben said.

"Please, just try them on for me. They are very pretty and soft," mom said.

Anna and Ben did not want to argue with mom. They took the shirts and went to the fitting room. They put on the shirts and looked at themselves in the mirror. They looked terrible. They felt terrible. They wanted to take off the shirts and run away.

They had an idea. They saw a window in the fitting room. It was open and had a ledge. They looked outside and saw the sky. It was blue and clear and had many birds. They wished they were birds. They wished they could soar in the air and be free.

They took off the shirts and threw them on the floor. They grabbed their planes and climbed on the ledge. They held their planes and jumped out of the window. They felt the wind on their faces and the sun on their hair. They smiled and laughed. They made their planes soar in the air and pretended they were pilots.

Mom heard their laughter and looked out of the window. She saw them flying with their planes. She was shocked and scared. She ran to the window and shouted.

"Anna! Ben! Come back! You can't fly! You'll fall!"

But Anna and Ben did not hear her. They did not see her. They only saw the sky and their planes. They were happy. They were soaring.

Anna and Ben were twins who liked to play in the garden. They had a big tree with green fruits that looked like balls. They were called limes. Anna and Ben liked to pick limes and squeeze them to make juice.

One day, they picked a lot of limes and filled a big jug with juice. They wanted to drink it, but it was too sour. They made faces and spit it out.

"Yuck! This juice is bad!" Anna complained.

"Me too! I don't like it!" Ben complained.

They saw their mom coming from the house. She had a smile on her face and a plate of cookies in her hands.

"Hi, kids! Do you want some cookies? They are sweet and soft and yummy!" she said.

Anna and Ben ran to their mom and grabbed the cookies. They forgot about the juice and the limes. They ate the cookies and made crumbs on the ground.

"Thank you, mom! These cookies are good!" Anna said.

"Me too! I like them!" Ben said.

They did not say please or sorry or share with their mom. They were greedy and rude.

Their mom was sad. She saw the jug of juice and the limes on the tree. She had an idea. She poured some juice in a glass and added some sugar and water. She stirred it well and tasted it. It was sweet and refreshing.

She gave the glass to Anna and Ben. They drank it and liked it.

"Wow! This juice is good!" Anna said.

"Me too! I like it!" Ben said.

They asked for more. Their mom said no.

"You had enough juice and cookies. You should not waste food or complain about it. You should be grateful and polite. And you should try new things. Sometimes, they are better than you think. Like this juice. It is made from the limes you picked. You just need to add some sugar and water to make it sweet. Do you understand?" she said.

Anna and Ben nodded. They felt sorry. They said sorry to their mom and hugged her. They said please and thank you and shared with her. They learned their lesson.

But it was too late. The limes on the tree were gone. They had picked them all. They could not make more juice. They could only drink water. They were thirsty and bored. They wished they had not complained and wasted the limes. They wished they had been more careful and delicate with the tree. They wished they had listened to their mom. They were unhappy.

The end.

Moral: Don't complain or waste food. Be grateful and polite. Try new things. Be careful and delicate with nature. Listen to your mom.

Lily and Tom were happy. They liked the cat and the kittens. They were gentle and careful. They petted them and played with them. They made new friends in the hay. They smiled.

Lily saw the sheet and had an idea. She wrapped the sheet around her like a cape and said, "I am a superhero and I will strike you with my power!" She ran towards Tom and tried to hit him with the sheet. Tom was scared and he ran away from Lily. He bumped into the table and knocked over a lamp. The lamp broke and made a loud noise.

Mom heard the noise and came to the room. She saw the broken lamp, the sheet on the floor, and Lily and Tom looking guilty. She was very angry and she said, "What have you done? You have made a big mess and broken the lamp! Why were you fighting?"

Lily and Tom felt sorry and they said, "We are sorry, Mom. We were fighting over the train and the sheet. We were angry and we did not share." Mom said, "You should not fight with each other. You are twins and you should love each other. You should share your toys and books and play nicely. Fighting only leads to trouble and sadness. Do you understand?" Lily and Tom nodded and they said, "We understand, Mom. We love each other and we will share. Can we hug and say sorry?" Mom smiled and she said, "Yes, you can. But first, you have to clean up the mess and help me fix the lamp." Lily and Tom agreed and they hugged and said sorry. They learned their lesson and they never fought over the train and the sheet again.

Lily and Ben were friends. They liked to play in the park. One day, they saw a big tree with red apples. Lily wanted to pick an apple, but Ben said no.

"Apples are not good. They are spicy and make your mouth hurt. Let's play with the ball instead," Ben said.

But Lily did not listen. She wanted to try an apple. She climbed the tree and picked a big red apple. She took a bite and smiled.

"Apples are not spicy. They are sweet and juicy. Try one, Ben. They are yummy," Lily said.

But Ben did not want to try. He ignored Lily and played with the ball. He kicked the ball hard and it flew away. He ran after the ball, but he could not find it. He looked everywhere, but the ball was gone.

He felt sad and lonely. He wished he had listened to Lily. He went back to the tree and saw Lily eating another apple. She looked happy and full.

"Lily, I'm sorry. I lost the ball. Can I have an apple, please?" Ben asked.

Lily looked at Ben and smiled. She picked another apple and gave it to Ben.

"Here, Ben. You can have an apple. Apples are good. They are not spicy. They are sweet and juicy. And they are better than balls. They don't fly away," Lily said.

Ben took the apple and bit it. He was surprised. The apple was not spicy. It was sweet and juicy. He liked it. He thanked Lily and hugged her.

"Lily, you are right. Apples are yummy. And you are a good friend. I'm sorry I ignored you. Can we play together?" Ben asked.

Lily nodded and hugged him back.

"Yes, Ben. We can play together. We can play with the apples. We can make a pile, or roll them, or toss them. Apples are fun. And so are you," Lily said.

They laughed and played with the apples. They forgot about the ball. They were happy. They were friends.

Sara and Ben were twins who liked to play with puzzles. They had many puzzles with different pictures of animals, cars, flowers and more. Sometimes they helped each other to solve the puzzles, and sometimes they had a race to see who could solve their own puzzle faster.

One day, they found a new puzzle in their toy box. It was a big puzzle with many pieces and a picture of a castle. Sara and Ben both wanted to solve the puzzle, but they only had one table to put the pieces on. They started to argue about who would get the puzzle first.

"I saw it first, so it's mine!" Sara said, grabbing the puzzle box.

"No, I saw it first, so it's mine!" Ben said, pulling the box from Sara.

They both pulled and pushed until the box opened and the pieces fell on the floor. Sara and Ben looked at the mess and felt sad. They had ruined their new puzzle.

They heard their mom coming and quickly picked up the pieces. They put them back in the box and hid it under the table. They hoped their mom would not notice.

"Hi, kids, what are you doing?" their mom asked, smiling.

"Nothing, mom, just playing," Sara and Ben said, trying to act normal.

Their mom looked at them and saw their guilty faces. She also saw a piece of the puzzle sticking out from under the table. She knew what had happened.

"Kids, did you fight over the puzzle?" she asked, gently.

Sara and Ben nodded, feeling ashamed.

"Why did you do that? You know you have to share and take turns," their mom said.

"We're sorry, mom, we just wanted to solve the puzzle," Sara and Ben said.

"Well, you can still solve the puzzle, but you have to do it together. It's more fun and easier to solve a puzzle with a friend than alone. And you have to be patient and respectful, not impatient and rude. Do you understand?" their mom said.

Sara and Ben nodded again, feeling sorry.

"Can we try again, mom?" Sara asked.

"Of course, but first you have to hug and say sorry to each other," their mom said.

Sara and Ben hugged and said sorry to each other. They felt better and smiled.

They took the puzzle box and opened it carefully. They spread the pieces on the table and started to look for the edges and corners. They worked as a team, helping each other to find the matching pieces. They talked and laughed and had fun. They solved the puzzle and saw the beautiful picture of the castle. They were proud and happy.

They showed their mom their finished puzzle and she praised them.

"See, kids, you did a great job. You solved the puzzle and you solved your problem. You learned to share and cooperate. I'm proud of you," their mom said.

Sara and Ben hugged their mom and thanked her. They learned their lesson and never fought over a puzzle again. They always played nicely and solved puzzles together. They were good twins.

Tom and Anna are twins. They like to play in the snow. One day, they see a big hill near their house. It is covered with white snow. They want to slide down the hill.

"Let's go, Tom!" Anna says. She grabs her red sled and runs to the hill. Tom follows her with his blue sled. They put their sleds on the snow and sit on them.

"Ready, set, go!" Tom shouts. They push their sleds and rush down the hill. They feel the cold wind on their faces and the icy snow under their sleds. They laugh and scream as they go faster and faster.

But the hill is too steep and the snow is too slippery. They cannot stop their sleds. They zoom past the end of the hill and fly into the air. They land on a soft pile of hay in a farm. They are not hurt, but they are surprised and scared.

"Wow, that was fun!" Anna says. She looks at Tom and smiles.

"Fun? That was scary!" Tom says. He looks at Anna and frowns.

They get up and dust off the hay from their clothes. They see a farmer coming towards them. He is holding a pitchfork and he looks angry.

"Hey, you kids! What are you doing here? You could have hurt my animals!" the farmer says. He points at his cows and sheep in the barn.

"Sorry, sir. We did not mean to. We were just sliding on the hill and we could not stop," Anna says. She holds Tom's hand and looks at the farmer with big eyes.

"Yeah, sorry, sir. We will not do it again," Tom says. He nods and looks at the farmer with big eyes.

The farmer sees their sleds and their faces. He softens his voice and his face.

"Well, I guess you did not know. But you have to be careful. The hill is too dangerous for sliding. And you have to ask permission before you enter someone's land. Do you understand?" the farmer says.

"Yes, sir. We understand. Thank you, sir," Anna and Tom say. They pick up their sleds and walk back to the hill.

They decide to slide on a smaller and safer hill. They still have fun, but they do not rush too much. They also remember to respect other people's land. They learn a lesson from their icy adventure.

Ben and Lily were twins who liked to play in the garden. One day, they saw a big peach tree with many ripe peaches. They wanted to pick some, but they were fearful of the bees that buzzed around the tree.

"Let's wait until the bees go to sleep," Ben said. "Then we can get some peaches."

"Okay," Lily agreed. "But how do we know when the bees are asleep?"

Ben thought for a moment. He remembered that his mom had told him that bees sleep at night, when it is dark. He looked at the sky and saw that the sun was still high.

"We have to wait until the sun goes down," he said. "Then it will be dark and the bees will sleep."

They decided to play with their toys until then. They had a lot of fun, but they also kept looking at the peach tree. They were hungry and curious.

When the sun started to set, they ran to the peach tree. They climbed on a low branch and reached for the peaches. They were juicy and sweet. They ate as many as they could.

"Yum, these are the best peaches ever!" Lily said.

"I know, right?" Ben said. "And we don't have to be fearful of the bees anymore. They are asleep now."

But they were wrong. The bees were not asleep. They were just resting. They heard the twins munching on their peaches and they got angry. They flew out of their hive and attacked the twins.

"Ow, ow, ow!" Ben and Lily cried. "The bees are stinging us!"

They dropped the peaches and jumped off the branch. They ran to their house, crying and rubbing their bumps. Their mom heard them and came out. She saw the bees and the peaches and understood what had happened.

She took them inside and put some ice on their bumps. She hugged them and said, "I'm sorry, my loves. You should have listened to me. Bees don't sleep at night. They just rest. They are awake and alert. You should never disturb them or take their food. They will defend themselves."

Ben and Lily nodded. They felt sorry and learned their lesson. They said, "We're sorry, mom. We won't do it again. We love you."

They kissed their mom and went to bed. They were still hungry, but they were too tired and sore to eat. They fell asleep, dreaming of peaches and bees.

Suddenly, a voice said, "That's a lovely zipper, Johnny." Johnny looked up to see his grandma standing there and smiled.

Grandma said, "Would you like to keep this zipper and make something special with it?"

Johnny was so excited and said, "Yes! I can make something lovely with it!"

Grandma smiled and said, "Okay, it's all yours. Take good care of it and remember how much I love you."

Johnny hugged Grandma and said, "I love you too!" He knew he would make something really special with the zipper and it would always remind him of his beloved grandma.

Billy was happy and he learnt a lesson. He knew he had to be careful and never to touch the saw again. He was getting wiser and wiser!

But the uncle forgot something important. He forgot to give them a special gift. When he remembered, he ran to his room and got it. It was a big box with a red bow. The niece and nephew were very excited. They opened the box and found new toys inside. They hugged their uncle and said, "Thank you!" They all played together and had a great day.

Once upon a time, there was a little independent bird named Bobo. He loved to fly in the wind and feel it on his wings. One day, Bobo met a big bird named Gogo. Gogo was very big and strong.

Bobo said to Gogo, "I can clap my wings very fast! Can you clap your wings too?" Gogo laughed and said, "I can clap my wings faster than you, little bird!" They decided to have a race to see who could clap their wings the fastest.

Bobo and Gogo started the race. They both clapped their wings very fast. Gogo was winning, but Bobo did not give up. He clapped his wings faster and faster. But then, a big wind came and blew Bobo away. Gogo won the race, but Bobo was lost and far away from home.

Bobo felt sad and scared. He tried to find his way back home, but the wind was too strong. In the end, Bobo could not find his way home and stayed lost forever.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim was a thoughtful boy who always helped his friends. One day, Tim saw a cat stuck in a tree. He wanted to help the cat come down from the tree.

Tim had an idea. He found a big bottle and filled it with water. He put the bottle under the tree and climbed up. Tim poured the water on the tree branch. The cat saw the water and jumped down to the ground. Tim's friends clapped and cheered for him.

The moral of the story is to always be thoughtful and try to help others when they need it. When you do good things for others, they will be happy, and you will be happy too.

Dory replied, "I feel dizzy, Nemo. I can't swim anymore."

Nemo knew he had to help his friend, so he swam around the shark and distracted it while Dory swam away. The shark followed Nemo, but he was too quick for the shark to catch.

After they escaped, Dory said, "Thank you, Nemo. You saved me from that sharp shark. I'm not dizzy anymore."

Nemo smiled and said, "That's what friends are for." And they continued their swim in the big blue ocean, happy to have each other.

As the days went by, Lily and Lumi would watch the flower grow bigger and bigger. They would talk to the flower and keep it company. One day, the flower bloomed fully and said, "Thank you, Lily and Lumi, for helping me grow!" Lily and Lumi smiled, happy to have a new friend in the wide garden.

Lisa felt bad for the bug. She decided to draw a nice flower for it. She used her pastels to make it very pretty. The bug came back and sat on the flower. It was happy now. Lisa showed her picture to her mom, and they both smiled.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She lived in a small house with her mom, dad, and her dog, Max. One day, Lily's mom said, "Lily, we will have a quiz today. It will be fun!" Lily was happy and could not wait.

Before the quiz, Lily's mom warned her, "Be careful, Lily. The quiz has a cold surprise." Lily did not know what that meant, but she wanted to find out. She played the quiz with Max and her mom. They had to find things in the house that were cold.

Lily found ice in the fridge, and Max found a cold toy. But when they found a cold box, they were not ready for the surprise. When they opened it, cold snow fell out! It was a fun mess. Lily's mom laughed, and they all played in the snow. The quiz was fun, just like her mom said.

One day, a little girl named Lily went to the park with her mom. She saw a big slide and wanted to try it. She climbed up the stairs and sat on the slide. But before she could slide down, she saw something shiny on the slide. It was a crown!

"Wow, a crown!" Lily said. "Maybe it belongs to a queen!"

She picked up the crown and put it on her head. She felt very happy and proud. She slid down the slide with the crown on her head. She smiled and waved to her mom.

"Look, mom, I'm a queen!" she shouted.

Her mom smiled and clapped. She was glad that Lily was having fun. She walked over to the slide and hugged Lily.

"You are a very pretty queen, Lily," she said. "But do you know who this crown really belongs to?"

Lily shook her head. She didn't know.

"This crown belongs to a very special queen," her mom said. "She is the queen of the bees. She lives in a hive with many other bees. They make honey and pollinate flowers. They are very busy and healthy."

Lily looked at the crown. She saw that it had tiny holes and yellow stripes. It looked like a bee.

"Oh, I see," she said. "This is a bee crown. I didn't know that bees had queens."

"Yes, they do," her mom said. "And they need their queen to lead them and take care of them. Without their queen, they would be very sad and confused. So we should return this crown to the queen bee. Do you know where we can find her?"

Lily thought for a moment. She remembered that she had seen a big tree with a hole in it. She had heard a buzzing sound coming from the hole.

"Maybe the queen bee lives in that tree," she said. "Let's go and see."

Lily and her mom walked to the tree. They saw many bees flying in and out of the hole. They also saw a sign that said "Bee Hive. Do Not Disturb."

"Look, mom, this is where the bees live," Lily said. "But how can we give the crown back to the queen bee?"

Her mom had an idea. She took a piece of string from her pocket and tied it to the crown. She gave the other end of the string to Lily.

"We can attach the crown to the string and lower it into the hole," she said. "Then the bees will see it and take it to their queen. But we have to be very careful and gentle. We don't want to hurt the bees or make them angry."

Lily nodded. She held the string and slowly lowered the crown into the hole. She watched as the bees flew around the crown. Some of them landed on it and touched it with their antennae. They seemed to recognize it and like it.

"Look, mom, the bees like the crown," Lily said. "They are taking it to their queen."

Her mom nodded. She saw that the bees were lifting the crown with their legs and wings. They carried it deeper into the hole. Soon, the crown disappeared from sight.

"Good job, Lily," her mom said. "You did a very kind thing. You made the queen bee happy. And you learned something new about bees. Aren't they amazing?"

Lily smiled. She felt happy too. She had helped the queen bee and had fun. She learned that bees had queens and crowns. She liked bees.

"Yes, mom, they are amazing," she said. "And so are you. You are my queen. And I love you."

She hugged her mom and kissed her cheek. Her mom hugged her back and kissed her forehead.

"I love you too, Lily," she said. "You are my princess. And you are amazing."

Tom and Mia are friends. They like to play pretend. Today, they pretend to be pirates. They have a big box for a ship, and a broom for a flag.

"Arr, matey, we are the best pirates ever!" Tom says. He wears a hat and an eye patch.

"Arr, yes, we are!" Mia agrees. She wears a scarf and a necklace.

They sail on the sea of their living room. They look for treasure and adventure. They sing pirate songs and laugh.

But then, they see a big shadow on the wall. It looks like a monster. It has big teeth and claws. It growls and roars.

"Ahoy, what is that?" Tom asks. He is scared.

"It is a dragon!" Mia says. She is brave. "We have to fight it!"

She grabs a pillow and throws it at the shadow. The shadow moves and makes a noise.

"Ow, stop that!" The shadow says. It is not a dragon. It is Tom's big brother, Sam. He was hiding behind the couch.

"Sam, you are not a dragon!" Tom says. He is angry.

"Sorry, I was just having fun. I wanted to see if you would believe me." Sam says. He is not serious.

"That is not fun, that is mean!" Mia says. She is not happy.

"Come on, don't be mad. It was just a joke." Sam says. He tries to smile.

"No, it was not. You ruined our game. Go away!" Tom says. He turns his back to Sam.

"Yeah, go away! We don't want to play with you!" Mia says. She turns her back to Sam too.

Sam feels bad. He knows he was wrong. He says sorry and leaves.

Tom and Mia hug. They are still friends. They decide to play something else. They believe in their imagination. They have fun.

Lily and Ben were best friends. They liked to play in the garden and make up stories. One day, they found a lime on the ground. It was green and round and smelled good.

"Let's plan a picnic with the lime," Lily said. "We can pretend it is a cake and share it with our toys."

"OK," Ben said. "But we need to find a place to have the picnic. Where should we go?"

Lily looked around and saw a big tree with a hole in it. "How about there?" she pointed. "It looks like a secret house. Maybe there are fairies inside."

Ben nodded. "Let's go. But we have to be careful. The tree might be old and have bugs."

They picked up the lime and their toys and walked to the tree. They put a blanket on the ground and set up their plates and cups. They cut the lime in half and gave each toy a piece. Then they each took a bite of their own piece.

"Yuck!" Lily and Ben said at the same time. The lime was sour and made their faces twist. They spit out the lime and made a funny noise.

They heard a giggle from inside the tree. They looked and saw a little girl with wings and a dress made of leaves. She was holding a basket of berries.

"Hello," she said. "I'm Flora, the fairy of the tree. I saw you plan your picnic and I wanted to surprise you. I'm sorry the lime was not sweet. It is good for making juice, but not for eating. Here, have some berries. They are sweet and juicy and good for you."

Lily and Ben smiled and thanked Flora. They took some berries and gave some to their toys. They ate and talked with Flora and learned about the tree and the garden. They had a lot of fun and became friends with Flora.

They learned that Flora was compassionate and kind. She helped the plants and animals in the garden and gave them gifts. She also liked to play and make up stories. She invited Lily and Ben to come back and visit her anytime.

Lily and Ben agreed. They hugged Flora and said goodbye. They took their toys and their blanket and walked back to their house. They decided to keep the lime as a souvenir of their picnic and their new friend. They put it on their shelf and smiled. They had a wonderful day.

Lily and Max are twins. They like to play with pastels. Pastels are soft and colorful. They can make pictures with them on paper.

One day, Lily and Max find a big box of pastels in the closet. They are very happy. They take the box to the living room and open it. There are many pastels inside. Some are new and some are old.

Lily picks a new pastel. It is pink. She likes pink. She starts to draw a flower on a white paper. Max picks an old pastel. It is brown. He does not like brown. He wants a new pastel too.

He looks at Lily's paper. He sees her pink flower. He likes it. He wants it. He reaches for Lily's pastel. Lily sees him. She does not want to share. She holds her pastel tight.

"Mine!" she says.

"No, mine!" he says.

They pull the pastel. They hear a snap. The pastel breaks in half. They both drop the pieces. They look at each other. They are sad. They have no pastel now.

They hear a voice. It is Mom. She comes to the living room. She sees the broken pastel. She sees the twins' faces. She knows what happened.

She picks up the pieces. She gives one to Lily and one to Max. She smiles.

"It's okay," she says. "You can still draw with them. You can make new colors. You can share. Sharing is nice."

Lily and Max look at the pieces. They look at Mom. They look at each other. They nod. They say sorry. They hug.

They take their pieces and start to draw again. They make new colors. They share. They are happy. They have pastels.

Tom and Jen are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a big parade. There are many people and animals and cars and flags. They want to join the parade.

"Let's march with them!" Tom says. He holds Jen's hand and runs to the parade.

"Wait, Tom!" Jen says. "We need a flag too!" She sees a red scarf on a bench. She picks it up and ties it around her waist.

"Now we are fine!" Jen says. She smiles and waves the scarf.

They march with the parade. They feel happy and proud. They see many things and hear many sounds. They do not see the man who owns the scarf. He is looking for it. He is angry and sad.

The man sees Tom and Jen. He sees his scarf on Jen's waist. He runs to them. He shouts at them.

"Hey, you! Give me back my scarf! That is mine!" He says.

Tom and Jen are scared. They did not know the scarf was his. They thought it was free. They stop marching. They let go of each other's hand.

"Sorry, sir. We did not know. We just wanted to march with the parade." Jen says. She unties the scarf and gives it to the man.

The man takes the scarf. He looks at Tom and Jen. He sees their faces. They are sorry and sad. He feels sorry too. He remembers when he was a child. He liked to march with parades too.

"It's okay, kids. I forgive you. You can keep the scarf. It looks fine on you." He says. He smiles and gives the scarf back to Jen.

"Really? Thank you, sir. You are very kind." Jen says. She ties the scarf around her waist again.

Tom and Jen hug the man. They thank him again. They hold each other's hand and run back to the parade. They march with the scarf. They feel happy and proud again. They see many things and hear many sounds. They do not see the man who waves at them. He is happy and proud too.

Lily liked to read books. She had many books with pictures and words. She read about animals, cars, fairies and more. She read every day and learned new things.

One day, she took her book and went to the park. She saw a big tree with many branches. She climbed up the tree and found a nice branch to sit on. She opened her book and started to read.

But then, she heard a loud noise. It was a crow. The crow was black and had a sharp beak. The crow flew to the branch where Lily was sitting and said, "Caw, caw, caw! This is my branch! Go away, go away, go away!"

Lily was scared and sad. She said, "Please, Mr. Crow, let me read my book. I like this branch. It is big and strong. I will not bother you. I will be quiet and read."

But the crow was rude. He said, "No, no, no! This is my branch! You are a bother. You are not quiet. You are a silly girl. Go away, go away, go away!"

He pecked at Lily's book and tore the pages. He pecked at Lily's hair and pulled the strands. He pecked at Lily's face and made her cry.

Lily was hurt and angry. She said, "Stop, stop, stop! You are a bad crow. You are mean and rude. You do not share. You do not care. Go away, go away, go away!"

She threw her book at the crow and hit him on the head. He said, "Ow, ow, ow! You are a bad girl. You are mean and rude. You do not play. You do not stay. Go away, go away, go away!"

He flew away from the branch and left Lily alone. Lily was sad and lonely. She picked up her book and saw the torn pages. She said, "I do not like this park. I do not like this tree. I do not like this crow. I want to go home. I want to read my book."

She climbed down the tree and ran to her mom. She hugged her mom and told her what happened. Her mom said, "I am sorry, Lily. That was a bad crow. He was mean and rude. He did not share. He did not care. He was not a friend. You are a good girl. You are kind and smart. You like to share. You like to care. You are a friend. I love you, Lily. Let's go home and read your book."

Lily smiled and said, "I love you, mom. Thank you, mom. Let's go home and read my book."

Tom was a little boy who liked to play with his toys. He had many cars, trains, and planes that he could zoom around his room. He also had a big teddy bear that he hugged every night. Tom loved his toys, but he did not like to clean them. He left them on the floor, on the bed, and on the table. He did not put them away in the box when he was done.

One day, his mom told him to take a shower. She said he was dirty and he needed to wash. Tom did not want to take a shower. He wanted to play more. He said, "No, mom, I don't want to take a shower. I want to play with my toys."

His mom said, "Tom, you have to take a shower. It is good for you. You will feel fresh and happy. And you have to clean your toys too. They are dusty and messy. You have to take care of them. They are your friends."

Tom did not listen to his mom. He ran to his room and locked the door. He lay on the floor and played with his toys. He made loud noises and pretended he was flying in the sky. He did not hear his mom knocking on the door. He did not hear the thunder outside. He did not see the dark clouds.

Soon, it started to rain. The rain was very heavy and strong. It made a lot of noise on the roof. It also made a hole in the roof. The water came through the hole and into Tom's room. It wet his toys and his bed. It made a big puddle on the floor. Tom was scared. He cried and shouted, "Mom, mom, help me! There is water in my room! My toys are wet! My bed is wet!"

His mom heard him and came to his room. She opened the door and saw the water. She was worried. She said, "Oh, Tom, what happened? Why did you lock the door? Why did you not take a shower? Why did you not clean your toys?"

Tom felt sorry. He said, "I'm sorry, mom. I was naughty. I did not listen to you. I did not want to take a shower. I did not want to clean my toys. I just wanted to play. But now I see I was wrong. I should have done what you said. I should have taken a shower. I should have cleaned my toys. I should have put them away. Now they are wet and dirty. And so am I."

His mom hugged him and said, "It's okay, Tom. I forgive you. But you have to learn from this. You have to do what is good for you. You have to take care of yourself and your things. You have to be responsible and respectful. You have to listen to me. I love you and I want you to be happy and healthy."

Tom nodded and said, "I love you too, mom. And I will do what you say. I will take a shower. I will clean my toys. I will put them away. I will be a good boy."

His mom smiled and said, "That's good, Tom. Come on, let's go to the bathroom. We will take a shower together. And then we will dry your toys and your bed. And then we will have some cookies and milk. How does that sound?"

Tom smiled and said, "That sounds great, mom. Thank you, mom. You are the best mom."

The end.

Moral value: The story teaches the value of obedience, cleanliness, and responsibility. It shows the consequences of not listening to parents, not taking care of oneself and one's belongings, and being careless. It also shows the importance of apologizing, forgiving, and learning from mistakes. It shows the love and care of parents and children.

He tried to strike some twigs and leaves with his beak, but they fell to the ground. He tried to strike some grass and feathers, but they flew away in the wind. He tried to strike some mud and stones, but they broke and splashed. He felt sad and tired.

Then he saw a squirrel named Red who lived in the same tree. Red was smart and knew how to make a nest. He had a cozy and warm nest with nuts and berries. He saw Blue and felt sorry for him.

He said to Blue, "Hello, friend. Do you need some help? I can show you how to make a nest. You just need to be patient and careful. Come, follow me."

Blue was happy and grateful. He followed Red and learned how to make a nest. He used some twigs and leaves, some grass and feathers, and some mud and stones. He struck them gently and firmly with his beak, and made a nice and sturdy nest.

He thanked Red and said, "You are very kind and helpful. You are a good friend. I am glad I met you."

Red smiled and said, "You are welcome, friend. You are brave and willing. You are a good friend too. I am glad you live here."

They became good friends and lived happily in the tree.

The moral of the story is: If you are clumsy and need help, do not be afraid to ask. If you are smart and can help, do not be proud to share. Friendship is more important than skill.

Lily was a regular cat. She liked to nap, chase mice, and scratch the sofa. But she had one special thing: she could pass through walls. She learned this when she was a kitten, and she used it to explore the house and the garden.

One day, she saw a big dog outside. The dog was barking and running around. Lily wanted to play with him, but she was afraid he would bite her. She decided to pass through the wall and sneak up behind him. She thought it would be fun to scare him.

She waited until the dog was near the wall, and then she passed through it. She pounced on his tail and said, "Meow!" The dog was very surprised. He turned around and saw Lily. He was not angry, he was happy. He said, "Woof! Who are you? You are a funny cat. Do you want to be my friend?"

Lily was also surprised. She expected the dog to be mean, but he was nice. She said, "Meow! I am Lily. I can pass through walls. Do you want to see?" The dog said, "Woof! Yes, please. That sounds amazing. How do you do that?"

Lily said, "Meow! I don't know. I just do it. Come, follow me." She passed through the wall again, and the dog followed her. He was amazed. He said, "Woof! This is so cool. Can we do it again?" Lily said, "Meow! Sure. Let's go to the kitchen. Maybe we can find some food."

They passed through the wall again, and went to the kitchen. They saw a bowl of milk on the table. Lily said, "Meow! Look, milk. My favorite. Do you want some?" The dog said, "Woof! No, thank you. I prefer bones. But you can have it." Lily jumped on the table and drank the milk. She said, "Meow! Thank you. You are a good friend. Do you want to play some more?" The dog said, "Woof! Yes, I do. But we have to be careful. The humans might see us. They don't like it when we pass through walls. They think we are ghosts."

Lily said, "Meow! Don't worry. We can be fast and quiet. Come on, let's go to the living room. There are some toys there." They passed through the wall again, and went to the living room. "OK, Lily, but be careful. Mama said some blueberries are bad and make us sick. We have to look for the good ones." Max said.

Lily nodded, but she was careless. She did not look at the blueberries well. She just grabbed the ones that looked big and juicy. She did not see that some of them were green and had spots.

"Yum, yum, these are so good!" Lily said, putting many blueberries in her mouth.

Max looked at her and saw the bad blueberries. He was scared.

"Lily, stop! Those are bad blueberries! Spit them out!" Max shouted.

But Lily did not listen. She was too busy eating. She did not feel the bad taste or the pain in her tummy. She just wanted more and more.

"Max, you are silly. These are the best blueberries ever. I dare you to eat some too!" Lily said, laughing.

Max shook his head. He did not want to eat the bad blueberries. He wanted to help Lily. He tried to take the blueberries from her hand, but she pushed him away.

"Go away, Max! These are mine! You are not my friend!" Lily said, angry.

Max was sad and scared. He did not know what to do. He ran to find Mama and tell her what happened. He hoped Mama could help Lily.

They see a jar of jam. It is red and sticky.

"Let's try this," Lisa says.

She takes out the jar of jam. She opens it easily.

"Yay, I did it," she says.

She smells the jam. It smells sweet.

"Can we eat it?" Tom asks.

Lisa nods. She takes a spoon from the drawer. She scoops some jam and puts it in her mouth.

"Mmm, it is good," she says.

She gives the spoon to Tom. He does the same.

"Mmm, it is good for me too," he says.

They eat more jam. They make a mess. They have jam on their faces, hands, and clothes.

They hear a noise. It is their mom. She is coming to the kitchen.

"Oh no, we are in trouble," Tom says.

They hide behind the refrigerator. They hope mom won't see them.

Mom comes to the kitchen. She sees the open refrigerator. She sees the jar of jam. She sees the spoon. She sees the mess.

She is not happy.

"Tom, Lisa, where are you?" she asks.

She looks around. She sees them behind the refrigerator.

She is not happy.

"Tom, Lisa, what are you doing?" she asks.

They come out. They look at mom. They are scared.

They try to explain.

"Mom, we were hungry. We wanted to eat something. We opened the refrigerator. We saw the jam. We ate some. It was good. We are sorry. We made a mess. We will clean it up. Please don't be mad," they say.

Mom listens. She understands. She is not happy, but she is not mad.

She sighs.

"Tom, Lisa, I know you were hungry. But you can't eat jam by itself. It is not good for you. It is too sweet. You need to eat regular food. Like bread, or cereal, or fruit. And you can't open the refrigerator by yourself. It is not safe. You could hurt yourself. Or spoil the food. Or waste the energy. You need to ask me first. Do you understand?" she says.

Tom and Lisa nod. They understand.

They are sorry.

They hug mom.

They say sorry again.

Mom hugs them back.

She says it is OK.

She says she loves them.

She says they need to clean up.

They say OK.

They clean up.

They eat regular food.

They are happy.

They are good.

Lily and Tom are twins. They like to play in the kitchen. They find a fork and a lock. They want to see what they can do with them.

"Look, Lily, I can put the fork in the lock," Tom says. He tries to turn the fork, but it does not move. "It is stuck. Help me, Lily."

Lily tries to pull the fork out of the lock, but it does not come out. "It is too hard, Tom. We need to ask Mom."

They run to find Mom. She is in the living room. She is reading a book. She sees the fork and the lock in Tom's hand.

"What are you doing with that, Tom?" Mom asks. She is not happy. "That is not a toy. That is a lock for the door. And that is a fork for eating. You could hurt yourself or break something."

"Sorry, Mom," Tom says. "We were just playing. We wanted to see if the fork can open the lock. But it did not work. It is stuck. Can you help us?"

Mom sighs. She takes the fork and the lock from Tom. She uses a key to open the lock. She frees the fork. She gives them back to Tom.

"Here you go, Tom. But please, do not play with these things again. They are not nice. They are dangerous. If you want to play, you can use your toys. They are nice. They are fun. They are safe. Do you understand?"

"Yes, Mom," Tom says. He feels sorry. He hugs Mom. "Thank you, Mom. You are nice. You are the best."

Lily hugs Mom too. "Yes, thank you, Mom. We love you."

Mom smiles. She hugs them back. "I love you too, my sweet twins. Now, go and play nicely. And be careful."

"Mom said we have to wait. They are not ready yet. They are too hard and sour," Sue said.

"I don't care. I want one now. They look yummy," Tim said. He reached for a tomato and pulled it off.

"Ow! Why did you do that? That was mean!" Tim said.

"You were mean first. You did not listen to Mom. You took a tomato that was not yours," Sue said.

They heard Mom coming. She saw the tomatoes on the ground and the juice on their clothes. She was not happy.

"What happened here? Why did you strike each other with tomatoes? That was very unusual and naughty. You wasted good food and made a mess," Mom said.

Tim and Sue felt sorry. They said they were sorry to Mom and to each other. Mom hugged them and said they had to clean up and help her make some tomato soup. They learned their lesson. They did not strike with tomatoes again.

Sara and Ben are playing in the park. They see a big ball on the grass. Sara runs to get it, but Ben is faster. He grabs the ball and kicks it hard. The ball flies in the air and strikes a fan that is hanging from a tree. The fan falls down and makes a loud noise.

"Ben, you are bad!" Sara says. "You broke the fan!"

Ben is scared. He does not want to get in trouble. He says, "I'm sorry, Sara. I did not mean to break the fan. It was an accident."

Sara is angry. She wants the ball. She says, "Give me the ball, Ben. It is my turn to play."

Ben does not want to give the ball. He says, "No, Sara. It is my ball. I found it first."

Sara and Ben start to fight. They pull and push each other. They do not see a man who is walking towards them. The man is the owner of the fan. He is not happy. He says, "Hey, you two! What are you doing? You broke my fan!"

Sara and Ben stop fighting. They look at the man. They are afraid. They say, "We're sorry, mister. We did not see your fan. We were playing with the ball."

The man looks at the fan. It is broken. He looks at the ball. It is his ball. He says, "This is my ball. You took my ball. You owe me a new fan."

Sara and Ben are sad. They do not have money to buy a new fan. They say, "We're sorry, mister. We don't have money. We can't buy you a new fan."

The man thinks for a moment. He sees that Sara and Ben are sorry. He says, "Well, I guess you didn't mean to break my fan. It was an old fan anyway. I don't need it. You can keep the ball. But you have to promise me something."

Sara and Ben are curious. They say, "What do we have to promise, mister?"

The man says, "You have to promise to share the ball. And to be nice to each other. And to be careful with other people's things. Can you do that?"

Sara and Ben nod. They say, "Yes, mister. We can do that. We promise."

The man smiles. He says, "Good. Then you can go and play. Have fun. And be good."

Sara and Ben are grateful. They say, "Thank you, mister. You are very kind. We're sorry for breaking your fan."

The man says, "You're welcome. And don't worry about the fan. It's okay. Now go and enjoy the ball."

Sara and Ben hug the man. They say, "Bye, mister. Have a nice day."

The man says, "Bye, kids. Have a nice day too."

Sara and Ben run to the grass. They play with the ball. They share the ball. They are nice to each other. They are careful with other people's things. They are happy.

Sara liked to draw with her pen. She drew flowers and stars and hearts on her paper. She was very modest and did not show her drawings to anyone. She was happy with her pen.

Tommy was a mean boy. He liked to tease Sara and make her cry. He saw her pen and wanted to take it. He thought her drawings were silly and ugly. He was not modest at all. He was proud and rude.

One day, Tommy sneaked up behind Sara and grabbed her pen. He laughed and ran away. He said, "This is my pen now. Your drawings are stupid. I will make better ones." He was very mean.

Sara was very sad and angry. She wanted her pen back. She chased Tommy and shouted, "Give me my pen! That is mine! You are a bad boy!" She was very brave.

Tommy did not listen. He kept running and drawing with Sara's pen. He drew snakes and spiders and monsters on the walls. He was very naughty. He did not care about Sara or the walls.

But Tommy did not see the big hole in the ground. He was too busy teasing Sara and drawing. He tripped and fell into the hole. He dropped Sara's pen. He hurt his leg and his head. He cried and screamed. He was very scared.

Sara saw Tommy in the hole. She felt sorry for him. She wanted to help him. She picked up her pen and ran to the hole. She said, "Are you okay? Do you need help?" She was very kind.

But Tommy did not say thank you. He did not say sorry. He said, "Give me my pen! That is mine! You are a stupid girl!" He was very foolish.

Sara was very hurt and angry. She did not want to help Tommy anymore. She said, "No, this is my pen. You are a mean boy. You deserve to be in the hole." She was very harsh.

She turned around and walked away. She left Tommy in the hole. She did not look back. She was very cold.

Anna and Ben were playing in the park with their dog, Spot. They liked to run and jump and slide and swing. Spot liked to chase and bark and fetch and wag. They were having a lot of fun.

But then they saw a big, dark house at the end of the street. It looked old and spooky. The windows were broken and the paint was peeling. There was a sign that said "Keep Out".

"Let's go see the house," Ben said. He was curious and brave. He took Spot's leash and started to walk towards the house.

"No, Ben, don't go!" Anna said. She was scared and worried. She did not like the house. She thought there might be monsters or ghosts inside. She grabbed Ben's hand and tried to pull him back.

"Come on, Anna, it's just a house," Ben said. He did not listen to Anna. He wanted to explore and see what was inside. He reached the door and pushed it open. It made a loud creak.

Anna gasped and Spot whimpered. They saw a dark and dusty hallway with cobwebs and spiders. They heard a strange noise from upstairs. It sounded like a moan or a growl.

"Ben, please, let's go back!" Anna said. She was very scared and wanted to leave. She tugged on Ben's hand and Spot's leash.

"OK, OK, fine," Ben said. He was a little scared too. He did not like the noise or the spiders. He closed the door and ran back to the park with Anna and Spot.

They decided to play somewhere else and never go near the house again. They were happy and safe. They hugged each other and Spot. They learned to be careful and listen to each other. They were good friends.

Tom and Lily wanted to bake a cake with Mom. They put on their aprons and washed their hands. Mom gave them a big bowl and a spoon. She said, "We need to measure the flour, sugar, butter and eggs. Can you help me?"

Tom nodded. He liked to measure things. He took the cup and filled it with flour. He poured it into the bowl. Lily wanted to do the same. She reached for the cup, but Tom pulled it away. He said, "No, Lily, it's my turn. I want to measure the sugar."

Lily frowned. She said, "That's not fair, Tom. I want to measure too. Let me have the cup."

Tom shook his head. He said, "No, Lily, you are too small. You might spill the sugar. I am bigger and reliable. I can measure better."

Lily was angry. She said, "No, Tom, you are not reliable. You are mean. You always insist on doing everything. Mom, tell Tom to share the cup."

Mom heard them arguing. She came over and said, "Tom, Lily, stop fighting. You can both measure. There is enough sugar for two cups. Tom, you can measure one cup and Lily can measure the other. Then you can take turns with the butter and the eggs. Baking a cake is more fun when we work together."

Tom and Lily looked at Mom. They felt sorry for being rude. They said, "Sorry, Mom. Sorry, Lily. Sorry, Tom." They smiled and hugged each other. They shared the cup and measured the sugar. They also shared the butter and the eggs. They stirred the bowl and poured the batter into the pan. Mom put the pan in the oven and set the timer. Tom and Lily waited for the cake to bake. They said, "Thank you, Mom. We love you. We love baking with you." Mom said, "I love you too, Tom and Lily. You are my sweet helpers."

Anna loved to sing. She sang all day, in the house, in the garden, in the car. She sang loud and happy. She wanted to be an opera singer, like the ones she saw on TV. She asked her mom and dad to take her to the opera, but they said it was too far and too expensive.

One day, Anna received a letter. It was from her aunt, who lived in the big city. She said she had a surprise for Anna. She invited her to come and stay with her for a week. She said she had tickets to the opera, and she wanted to take Anna with her. Anna was so excited. She packed her bag and hugged her mom and dad. She said goodbye to her dog and her cat. She got on the train with her aunt and went to the big city.

The big city was very different from Anna's home. It was noisy and crowded and busy. It was also very cold and icy. Anna saw snow for the first time. She liked to touch it and make snowballs. But she also missed her mom and dad and her pets. She felt lonely and scared. She told her aunt how she felt. Her aunt hugged her and said, "I know, sweetie. It's hard to be away from home. But you will see them soon. And you will have a wonderful time at the opera. You will love it, I promise."

The next day, they went to the opera. Anna wore a pretty dress and a warm coat. Her aunt gave her a pair of binoculars to see better. They entered a big and beautiful building, with red curtains and golden lights. They found their seats and waited for the show to start. Anna looked around and saw many people, dressed in fancy clothes and jewels. She felt nervous and shy. She wondered if she would like the opera.

The opera began. Anna heard the music and the singing. She was amazed. The singers had such powerful and beautiful voices. They sang in a language she did not understand, but she could feel the emotions. They sang about love and hate, joy and sorrow, life and death. They wore colorful costumes and moved on a big stage, with different sets and props. Anna was fascinated. She forgot about her home and her fears. She felt like she was in another world. She used her binoculars to see the singers up close. She smiled and clapped and cheered. She loved the opera.

After the opera, her aunt took her to a nice restaurant. They had ice cream and cake. They talked about the opera and what they liked best. Anna thanked her aunt for the surprise. She said it was the best gift ever. Her aunt smiled and said, "You're welcome, my dear. I'm glad you enjoyed it. You have a wonderful talent for singing. You can be an opera singer if you want to. But you have to work hard and practice a lot. And you have to be brave and confident. And you have to remember that no matter where you go or what you do, you always have a home and a family who love you."

Anna nodded and hugged her aunt. She felt happy and proud. She learned a lot from the opera. She learned about different cultures and languages and stories. She learned about art and beauty and expression. She learned about herself and her dreams. She learned that the world was big and wonderful, but also cold and icy. She learned that she could explore and enjoy the world, but also miss and appreciate her home. She learned that she could sing and love the opera, but also be a good and grateful niece. She learned that life was like an opera, full of music and drama, but also of lessons and values. She learned that the opera was a gift, but also a challenge. She learned that she was a singer, but also a child.
